The CMA may disregard matters raised by the appellant if it thinks it necessary to do so for the purpose of securing that an appeal under section 19A is determined within the period allowed under section 19D, unless the matters were raised by the appellant—
at the time of the application under paragraph 1 for permission to appeal, or
in an application under paragraph 6 for a direction.

The CMA may disregard matters raised by an intervener if it thinks it necessary to do so for the purpose of securing that an appeal under section 19A is determined within the period allowed under section 19D, unless the matters were raised by the intervener—
at the time of the application for permission to intervene under paragraph 4, or
in an application under paragraph 6 for a direction.
This paragraph applies where the CMA decides to remit a matter that is the subject of an appeal under section 19A to the CAA for reconsideration and decision.

Where, on reconsidering the matter, the CAA decides to modify a licence, the notice under section 11A(5) in respect of the modification may, with the agreement of the licence holder, specify a date falling—
before the end of the period of six weeks beginning with the date on which the notice is published, but
on or after the date on which the decision that was the subject of the appeal took effect or would have taken effect but for its suspension under this Schedule.
This paragraph applies where the CMA decides to substitute its own decision for a decision of the CAA that is the subject of an appeal under section 19A.
The decision of the CMA has effect as if made by the CAA except that—
section 11A(5) does not apply;
an appeal may not be brought against it under section 19A.
Any modification of a licence effected by the CMA takes effect from the date specified by the CMA.
The CMA may, with the agreement of the licence holder, specify a date falling—
before the date on which the order containing its decision is published, but
on or after the date on which the decision that was the subject of the appeal took effect or would have taken effect but for its suspension under this Schedule.
This paragraph applies to—
an authorised member of the CMA with the function of determining an application for permission to appeal under section 19A;
a group with the function of determining an appeal under that section.

The member or group must not have regard to any matter, information or evidence raised or provided by the CAA if it was not considered by the CAA in making the decision that is the subject of the application or the appeal, unless the member or group considers that—
the CAA could not reasonably have been expected to consider the matter, information or evidence when making that decision, and
the matter, information or evidence is likely to have an important effect on the outcome of the application or appeal, either by itself or taken together with other matters, information or evidence.

The member or group must not have regard to any matter, information or evidence raised or provided by a person other than the CAA if it was not considered by the CAA in making the decision that is the subject of the application or appeal, unless the member or group considers that—

the person or a relevant connected person could not reasonably have raised the matter with the CAA, or provided the information or evidence to the CAA, during the period in which the CAA was making that decision, and
the matter, information or evidence is likely to have an important effect on the outcome of the application or appeal, either by itself or taken together with other matters, information or evidence.

Where the member or group has regard to any matter, information or evidence in reliance on sub-paragraph (2) or (3), those sub-paragraphs do not prevent the member or group having regard to further matters, information or evidence raised or provided in response to it if the member or group considers that the further matter, information or evidence is likely to have an important effect on the outcome of the application or appeal, either by itself or taken together with other matters, information or evidence.
In sub-paragraph (3) “

”, in relation to a person who raises or provides a matter, information or evidence, means a person who was connected to that person at any time during the period in which the CAA was making the decision that is the subject of the application or appeal.
References in this paragraph to the period in which the CAA was making a decision are to the period—
beginning with the publication of a notice under section 11A(1) proposing to make the modification, and
ending with the publication of a notice under section 11A(5) in relation to that modification.
The CMA may by notice require a person to produce to it documents specified or described in the notice that are in the person's custody or under the person's control.
In this paragraph “
” means anything in which information is recorded.
The notice may require the production of documents—
at a time and place specified in the notice;
in a form and manner specified in the notice.

The notice may not require a person to produce documents that the person could not be compelled to provide in evidence in civil proceedings before the High Court or, in Scotland, the Court of Session.
A notice under this paragraph may be given on behalf of the CMA by an authorised member of the CMA.
For the purposes of this Schedule the following persons may hold an oral hearing and take evidence on oath—
an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 1 for permission to appeal;
an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 4 for permission to intervene;
an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 6 for a direction;
a group with the function of determining an appeal under section 19A.
In the course of holding such a hearing and taking such evidence, a person or group described in sub-paragraph (1) may administer oaths.
An authorised member of the CMA may by notice require a person—
to attend at a time and place specified in the notice, and
at that time and place, to give evidence to a member or group described in sub-paragraph (1).
At an oral hearing, the member or group conducting the hearing may require the following persons to give evidence or to make representations—
the applicant, the appellant or any intervener (if present);
a person attending a hearing as a representative of the applicant, the appellant, an intervener or the CAA.
Subject to sub-paragraph (6), a person who gives oral evidence at the hearing may be cross-examined by or on behalf of—
the appellant;
an intervener;
the CAA.
Such a person may be cross-examined by or on behalf of an intervener only with the leave of the member or group conducting the hearing.
If the applicant, the appellant, an intervener or a representative of any such person or the CAA is not present at a hearing—
there is no requirement to give notice to that person under sub-paragraph (3);
the member or group conducting the hearing may determine the application or appeal without hearing that person's evidence or representations.
A person may not be required under this paragraph to give evidence that the person could not be compelled to give in civil proceedings before the High Court or, in Scotland, the Court of Session.

Where a person is required under this paragraph to attend at a place more than 16 kilometres from the person's place of residence, an authorised member of the CMA must arrange for the person to be paid the necessary expenses of attendance.
A notice under this paragraph may be given on behalf of the CMA by an authorised member of the CMA.
The CMA may by notice require a person to produce a written statement with respect to a matter specified in the notice—
to an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 1 for permission to appeal;
to an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 4 for permission to intervene;
to an authorised member of the CMA considering an application under paragraph 6 for a direction;
to a group with the function of determining an appeal under section 19A.
The notice may require the written statement—
to be produced at the time and place specified in the notice;
to be verified by a statement of truth.
Where a notice requires a written statement to be verified by a statement of truth, the written statement may be disregarded unless it is so verified.

A person may not be required under this paragraph to produce a written statement about a matter if the person could not be compelled to give evidence about that matter in civil proceedings before the High Court or, in Scotland, the Court of Session.
A notice under this paragraph may be given on behalf of the CMA by an authorised member of the CMA.
Where permission to appeal is granted under paragraph 2, the CMA may commission expert advice with respect to any matter raised by—
the appellant,
an intervener, or
the CAA.

Emphasis.Addition: Enforcement of requirements in relation to evidence etc

Text.Addition: This paragraph applies where a person—
fails to comply with a notice under paragraph 17, 18 or 19,
fails to comply with any other requirement imposed under paragraph 17, 18 or 19,
in complying with a notice under paragraph 19, makes a statement that is false or misleading in a material respect, or
in providing information verified by a statement of truth required by appeal rules under paragraph 23, provides information that is false or misleading in a material respect.
An authorised member of the CMA may certify to the appropriate court—
the failure,
the fact that the person has made a false or misleading statement in circumstances described in sub-paragraph (1)(c), or
the fact that the person has provided false or misleading information in circumstances described in sub-paragraph (1)(d).
The appropriate court may inquire into a certified failure or act and, if it does so, must hear—
any witness against the person;
any witness on behalf of the person;
any statement in the person's defence.
The appropriate court may punish the person as if the person had been guilty of contempt of court if it is satisfied that—
the certified failure or act took place, and
the person did not have a reasonable excuse for the failure or act.
Where the person is a body corporate, the appropriate court may punish any director or other officer of that body, either instead or as well as punishing the body.
In this paragraph—
“the appropriate court”—
in relation to England and Wales and Northern Ireland, means the High Court;
in relation to Scotland, means the Court of Session;
”, in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, means a member of the body.
An application under paragraph 1 for permission to appeal may be withdrawn only with the consent of the CMA.
After an application for permission to appeal is granted, the appeal may be withdrawn only with the consent of the CMA.
An application under paragraph 4 for permission to intervene may be withdrawn only with the consent of the CMA.
After an application for permission to intervene is granted, the intervener may withdraw from the appeal only with the consent of the CMA.
For the purposes of sub-paragraphs (1) to (4), the consent of the CMA may be given by an authorised member of the CMA.
Where the CMA has consented, the person wishing to withdraw the application or appeal, or withdraw as an intervener, may give notice of withdrawal to the CMA.
An application under paragraph 6 for a direction suspending the effect of a decision may be withdrawn at any time by giving notice of withdrawal to the CMA.
Withdrawal of an application under this Schedule or of an appeal, or as an intervener in an appeal, has effect when the notice of withdrawal is given to the CMA.
A person giving notice of withdrawal to the CMA must send a copy of the notice to the CAA.
The CAA must—
publish the notice;
send a copy of it to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (11) (other than the person who gave the notice).
Those persons are—
the holder of the licence that is the subject of the application or appeal;
any other person with a qualifying interest in the decision that is the subject of the application or appeal;
any owners or operators of aircraft that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of prescribed aerodromes that the CAA considers appropriate.
The CMA Board may make rules regulating the conduct and disposal of appeals.
The rules may include provision supplementing the provisions of this Schedule in relation to any application, notice, hearing or requirement for which this Schedule provides.
The rules may, in particular, include—
provision requiring an application to be accompanied by information specified in the rules;
provision requiring such information to be verified by a statement of truth;
provision requiring an applicant to provide the CAA with information specified in the rules;
provision imposing time limits or other restrictions on the taking of evidence at an oral hearing;
provision imposing time limits or other restrictions on the making of representations or observations at such a hearing.
The rules may make different provision for different purposes.
Before making rules under this paragraph the CMA Board must consult any persons that it considers appropriate.
The CMA Board must publish the rules made under this paragraph.

Where an application under this Schedule or an appeal is withdrawn, an authorised member of the CMA may make any order that the member thinks fit requiring the parties to the application or appeal to make payments to each other and to the CMA in respect of costs incurred in connection with the application or appeal.
A group that determines an appeal must make an order requiring the payment to the CMA of the costs incurred by the CMA in connection with the appeal.
Subject to sub-paragraph (4), an order under sub-paragraph (2) must require those costs to be paid—
where the appeal is allowed in full, by the CAA;
where the appeal is dismissed in full, by the appellant;
where the appeal is allowed in part, by the appellant and the CAA in such proportions as the group considers appropriate.
The order may require an intervener in the appeal to pay such proportion of those costs (if any) as the group considers appropriate.

A group that determines an appeal may make any order that it thinks fit requiring one party to the appeal to make payments to another in respect of costs reasonably incurred by the other party in connection with the appeal.
A person who is required to make a payment by an order under this paragraph must comply with the order before the end of the period of 28 days beginning with the day after the making of the order.
If that person does not do so, the unpaid balance carries interest at a rate specified in the order or determined in accordance with it.

In this paragraph, references to an intervener in an appeal, and to a party to an appeal, include a person who was granted permission to intervene in an appeal and subsequently withdrew from the appeal.

Emphasis.Addition: Secretary of State's power to modify time limits

Text.Addition: The Secretary of State may by regulations modify any period of time specified in this Schedule.

Where the CAA, the CMA or an authorised member of the CMA is required by this Schedule to publish something or send a copy of something and this Schedule does not specify a time for doing so, it must be published or sent as soon as practicable.
In this Schedule—
” means an appeal under section 19A;
” has the meaning given in sub-paragraph (2);
” and “
” have the same meaning as in Schedule 4 to the Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013;
”, in relation to an appeal, means a person who has been granted permission to intervene in the appeal and who has not withdrawn from the appeal;
” has the meaning given in section 19A(3);

”, in relation to the production of a statement or in relation to information provided by a person, means a statement that the person producing that statement or providing that information believes the facts contained in the statement or the information to be true.
In this Schedule “authorised member of the CMA”—

in relation to a power exercisable in connection with an appeal, application or direction in respect of which a group has been constituted by the chair of the CMA under Schedule 4 to the Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013, means a member of that group who has been authorised by the chair of the CMA to exercise that power; and
in relation to a power exercisable in connection with an appeal, application or direction in respect of which a group has not been so constituted by the chair of the CMA, means—
any member of the CMA Board who is also a member of the CMA panel, or
any member of the CMA panel authorised by the Secretary of State (whether generally or specifically) to exercise the power in question.
For the purposes of this Schedule and sections 19D and 19E, a person has a qualifying interest in a decision that is the subject of an appeal or an application under this Schedule if—
the person has been granted permission to appeal against the decision and has not withdrawn the appeal,
the person has applied for permission to appeal against the decision and the application has not been withdrawn or refused,
the person has been granted permission to intervene in an appeal against the decision and the appeal has not been withdrawn,
the person has applied for permission to intervene in an appeal against the decision and the application has not been withdrawn or refused, or
the person has applied for a direction under paragraph 6, the application has not been withdrawn or refused and any direction made in response to the application has not been withdrawn.

Title.Addition: Enforcement of duties under section 8 and licence conditions

Text.Addition: The CAA may give a notice under this paragraph (a “contravention notice”) to a licence holder if it has reasonable grounds for believing that the licence holder is contravening, or has contravened, a Chapter 1 requirement.
In this Schedule “
”, in relation to a licence holder, means—
a duty imposed on the licence holder by section 8, or
a licence condition of the licence holder's licence.
A contravention notice must—
specify the Chapter 1 requirement and contravention in respect of which it is given;
explain the action that the CAA may take under this Schedule in connection with the contravention;
explain that representations may be made about the matters in the notice before the end of the period specified in the notice.
The CAA must specify a period of not less than 30 days beginning with the day on which the contravention notice is given, subject to sub-paragraph (5).
The CAA may specify a shorter period in a contravention notice given in respect of a repeated contravention.

A contravention notice is given to a licence holder in respect of a repeated contravention if, in the period of two years ending with the day on which the notice is given, the CAA did one or more of the following in respect of a contravention by the licence holder of the same Chapter 1 requirement—
gave the licence holder a contravention notice;
gave the licence holder an enforcement order;
gave the licence holder an urgent enforcement order;
imposed a penalty on the licence holder under paragraph 9 or 10.
The CAA may extend the period specified in a contravention notice given to a licence holder on one or more occasions by giving a notice to that licence holder.
The CAA may withdraw a contravention notice given to a licence holder at any time by giving a notice to the licence holder that includes its reasons for doing so.
As soon as practicable after giving a notice under sub-paragraph (1), (7) or (8), the CAA must—
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
A contravention notice given in respect of a contravention that is or was a continuing contravention must specify the period of contravention in respect of which it is given.
In this Schedule “
”, in relation to a contravention notice, means—
the period specified in the contravention notice for making representations;
where the period has been extended in accordance with sub-paragraph (7), the extended period.

If the CAA gives a licence holder a contravention notice or an urgent enforcement order (see paragraph 5) in respect of a contravention, it may not subsequently give the licence holder a contravention notice in respect of the same contravention.
Sub-paragraph (1) does not apply if—
the CAA withdraws the first contravention notice without imposing a penalty on the person under paragraph 9, or
the CAA revokes the urgent enforcement order without imposing a penalty on the licence holder under paragraph 10.
Sub-paragraph (1) does not prevent the CAA giving a licence holder more than one contravention notice, or a contravention notice and urgent enforcement order, in respect of—
contraventions of the same Chapter 1 requirement in different ways, or
contraventions of the same Chapter 1 requirement at different times or during different periods.
The CAA may give an order under this paragraph (an “enforcement order”) to a licence holder if—
it has given the licence holder a contravention notice (and has not withdrawn it),
the representation period has ended,
it has considered any representations made about the matters in the contravention notice before the end of that period (and not withdrawn), and
sub-paragraph (2) or (3) is satisfied.

This sub-paragraph is satisfied if the CAA has determined that the licence holder is contravening a Chapter 1 requirement specified in the contravention notice in one or more of the ways specified in the notice.
This sub-paragraph is satisfied if the CAA has determined that the licence holder—
has contravened a Chapter 1 requirement specified in the contravention notice in one or more of the ways specified in the notice, and
did not, before the end of the representation period, take all of the appropriate steps mentioned in sub-paragraph (6)(b).
An enforcement order must—
specify the Chapter 1 requirement and contravention in respect of which it is given;
require the licence holder to take any appropriate steps that are specified in the order;
specify a reasonable period within which the steps must be taken;
give the CAA's reasons for giving the order.
As soon as practicable after giving an enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish the order;
send a copy of the order to—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
In this paragraph “
”, in relation to a contravention of a Chapter 1 requirement, means steps that the CAA has determined are appropriate—
for complying with the requirement, and
for remedying the consequences of the contravention.
The CAA may—
modify an enforcement order with the agreement of the licence holder to whom it was given, or
revoke an enforcement order.
Before modifying or revoking the order, the CAA must—
publish a notice in relation to the proposed modification or revocation;
send a copy of the notice to the licence holder to whom the order was given;
consider any representations made about the proposal in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
The notice under sub-paragraph (2) must—
state that the CAA proposes to modify or revoke the order;
specify the proposed modification (if relevant);
give the CAA's reasons for the modification or revocation;
specify a reasonable period for making representations.
As soon as practicable after modifying or revoking an enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish a notice giving details of the modification or revocation;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (5).
The persons are—
the licence holder to whom the enforcement order was given;
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
The CAA may give an order under this paragraph (an “urgent enforcement order”) to a licence holder if sub-paragraph (2) or (3) is satisfied.
This sub-paragraph is satisfied if the CAA has reasonable grounds for believing that—
the licence holder is contravening, or has contravened, a Chapter 1 requirement,
the contravention has resulted in, or creates an immediate risk of, a serious economic or operational problem—
for owners or operators of aircraft, or
for owners or managers of aerodromes, and
it is appropriate to give an urgent enforcement order to prevent, remove or reduce that problem or risk.
This sub-paragraph is satisfied if the CAA has reasonable grounds for believing that—
the licence holder is likely to contravene a Chapter 1 requirement,
the contravention is likely to result in, or create an immediate risk of, a problem described in sub-paragraph (2)(b), and
it is appropriate to give the urgent enforcement order to prevent, or reduce the likelihood of, that problem or risk arising.
An urgent enforcement order must—
specify the Chapter 1 requirement and the contravention in respect of which it is given;
require the licence holder to take any appropriate steps that are specified in the order;
specify a reasonable period within which the steps must be taken;
give the CAA's reasons for giving the order.
As soon as practicable after giving an urgent enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish the order;
send a copy of the order to—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
In this paragraph “appropriate steps”—
in relation to a contravention of a Chapter 1 requirement that has occurred or is occurring, means steps that the CAA has determined are appropriate—
for complying with the requirement, and
for remedying the consequences of the contravention;
in relation to a contravention of a Chapter 1 requirement that is likely to occur, means steps that the CAA has determined are appropriate for securing that the contravention does not occur.
As soon as practicable after giving an urgent enforcement order, the CAA must—
confirm the order, or
revoke the order (see paragraph 7).
The CAA may confirm an urgent enforcement order with or without modifications.
The CAA may confirm an urgent enforcement order given in reliance on paragraph 5(2) only if it has determined that—
the licence holder is contravening, or has contravened, a Chapter 1 requirement specified in the order in one or more of the ways specified in the order,
the contravention has resulted in, or creates an immediate risk of, a problem described in paragraph 5(2)(b), and
it is appropriate to confirm the urgent enforcement order, with any modifications, to prevent, remove or reduce that problem or risk.
The CAA may confirm an urgent enforcement order given in reliance on paragraph 5(3) only if—
it has determined that paragraphs (a) to (c) of sub-paragraph (3) of this paragraph are satisfied, or
it has determined that—
the licence holder is likely to contravene a Chapter 1 requirement specified in the order in one or more of the ways specified in the order,
the contravention is likely to result in, or create an immediate risk of, a problem described in paragraph 5(2)(b), and
it is appropriate to confirm the urgent enforcement order, with any modifications, in order to prevent, or reduce the likelihood of, that problem or risk arising.
Before confirming an urgent enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish a notice in relation to the proposal to confirm the order;
send a copy of the notice to the licence holder to whom the order was given;
consider any representations made about the proposal in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
The notice under sub-paragraph (5) must—
state that the CAA proposes to confirm the order;
specify any proposed modifications of the order;
give the CAA's reasons for confirming the order and for any modifications;
specify a reasonable period for making representations.
As soon as practicable after confirming an urgent enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish a notice giving details of the confirmation, including any modifications of the order;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (8).
Those persons are—
the licence holder to whom the urgent enforcement order was given;
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.

Emphasis.Addition: Urgent enforcement order: modification and revocation

Text.Addition: The CAA may—
modify an urgent enforcement order with the agreement of the licence holder to whom it was given, or
revoke an urgent enforcement order.
Before modifying or revoking the order, the CAA must—
publish a notice in relation to the proposed modification or revocation;
send a copy of the notice to the licence holder;
consider any representations made about the proposal in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
The notice under sub-paragraph (2) must—
state that the CAA proposes to modify or revoke the order;
specify the proposed modification (if relevant);
give the CAA's reasons for the modification or revocation;
specify a reasonable period for making representations.
As soon as practicable after modifying or revoking an urgent enforcement order, the CAA must—
publish a notice giving details of the modification or revocation;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (5).
Those persons are—
the licence holder to whom the urgent enforcement order was given;
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
Nothing in this paragraph restricts, or applies in relation to the exercise of, the CAA's power under paragraph 6 to modify an urgent enforcement order when confirming the order.
A licence holder who is given an enforcement order must comply with it (unless it is revoked).
The obligation to comply with an enforcement order is a duty owed to every person who may be affected by a contravention of a requirement of the order.
A licence holder who is given an urgent enforcement order must comply with it, whether or not it has been confirmed (unless it is revoked).
The obligation to comply with an urgent enforcement order that has been confirmed is a duty owed to every person who may be affected by a contravention of a requirement of the order.
Where a duty is owed to a person under sub-paragraph (2) or (4), the following are actionable by the person—
a breach of the duty that causes the person to sustain loss or damage;
an act that—
by inducing a breach of the duty or interfering with its performance, causes that person to sustain loss or damage, and
is done entirely or partly for achieving that result.

In proceedings brought against a licence holder by virtue of sub-paragraph (5), it is a defence for the licence holder to show that it took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid contravening the requirements of the order.
The CAA may enforce the duties under sub-paragraphs (1) and (3)—
in civil proceedings for an injunction,
in civil proceedings in Scotland for an interdict or for specific performance of a statutory duty under section 45 of the Court of Session Act 1988, or
in civil proceedings for any other appropriate remedy or relief.
Enforcement of a duty under sub-paragraph (1) or (3) by the CAA does not prejudice any rights a person may have by virtue of sub-paragraph (5).

Emphasis.Addition: Penalty for contravention of Chapter 1 requirement

Text.Addition: The CAA may impose a penalty on a licence holder if—
it has given the licence holder a contravention notice (and has not withdrawn it),
the representation period has ended,
it has considered any representations made about the matters in the contravention notice before the end of that period (and not withdrawn), and
it has determined that the licence holder is contravening, or has contravened, a Chapter 1 requirement specified in the notice in one or more of the ways specified in the notice.
If the contravention notice specifies more than one contravention, the CAA may impose a separate penalty under this paragraph for each contravention.
If the contravention notice specifies more than one period of contravention, the CAA may impose a separate penalty under this paragraph for each period.
The CAA may impose a penalty on a licence holder if it has determined that the licence holder is contravening, or has contravened, a requirement of—
an enforcement order, or
an urgent enforcement order that has been confirmed.
Before imposing a penalty on a licence holder under paragraph 9 or 10 the CAA must—
give the licence holder a notice about the proposed penalty;
publish the notice as soon as practicable;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (3);
consider any representations made about the proposed penalty in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
A notice under sub-paragraph (1) must—
state that the CAA proposes to impose a penalty;
state the proposed amount of the penalty;
specify the requirement that the CAA has determined is being or has been contravened;
specify the act or omission that the CAA has determined constitutes a contravention of the requirement;
where the penalty would be imposed under paragraph 10, specify the Chapter 1 requirement in respect of which the enforcement order or urgent enforcement order (as the case may be) was given.
The persons are—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
In the case of a penalty calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount (see paragraph 13(2)), a notice must specify—
the day on which daily amounts would begin to accumulate;
the day on which, or the circumstances in which, they would cease to accumulate.

The period specified in a notice under sub-paragraph (1) for making representations must be a period of not less than 21 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given to the licence holder.
Before varying the proposed amount of a penalty, the CAA must—
give the licence holder on whom the penalty is to be imposed a notice about the proposed variation;
publish the notice as soon as practicable;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (3);
consider any representations made about the proposed variation in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
In the case of a penalty calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount (see paragraph 13(2)), the reference in sub-paragraph (6) to varying the proposed amount includes—
varying the day on which daily amounts would begin to accumulate;
varying the day on which, or the circumstances in which, they would cease to accumulate.
The notice under sub-paragraph (6) must—
specify the proposed variation;
give the CAA's reasons for the proposed variation.

The period specified in a notice under sub-paragraph (6) for making representations must be a period of not less than 21 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given to the licence holder.
The CAA may withdraw a notice under sub-paragraph (1) or (6) at any time by giving notice to the licence holder on whom it proposed to impose the penalty.
As soon as practicable after giving a notice under sub-paragraph (10), the CAA must—
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (3).
As soon as practicable after imposing a penalty under paragraph 9 or 10 the CAA must—
give a notice to the licence holder on whom the penalty is imposed;
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (3).
The notice must—
state that the CAA has imposed a penalty;
state the amount of the penalty;
specify the requirement that the CAA has determined is being or has been contravened;
specify the act or omission that the CAA has determined constitutes a contravention of the requirement;
where the penalty is imposed under paragraph 10, specify the Chapter 1 requirement in respect of which the enforcement order or urgent enforcement order (as the case may be) was given;
specify a reasonable period within which the penalty must be paid or reasonable periods within which different portions of the penalty must be paid.
The persons are—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
In the case of a penalty calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount (see paragraph 13(2)), the notice must specify—
the day on which the daily amounts begin to accumulate;
the day on which, or the circumstances in which, they cease to accumulate.
As soon as practicable after daily amounts cease to accumulate, the CAA must—
give a notice to the licence holder on whom the penalty was imposed confirming the day on which they ceased to accumulate;
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (3).
The amount of a penalty imposed on a person under paragraph 9 or 10 must be the amount that the CAA determines to be—
appropriate, and
proportionate to the contravention for which it is imposed.
The penalty may consist of either or both of the following—
a fixed amount (see paragraph 14);
a daily amount (see paragraph 15).
In determining the amount of a penalty, the CAA must have regard, in particular, to—
any representations made to it in a period specified in a notice proposing to give a penalty under paragraph 11(1) or (6) (and not withdrawn);
any steps taken by the licence holder on whom the penalty is to be imposed towards complying with—
the requirement specified in the notice under paragraph 11(1) by virtue of paragraph 11(2)(c), and
where the penalty is to be imposed under paragraph 10, the Chapter 1 requirement specified in the notice under paragraph 11(1) by virtue of paragraph 11(2)(e);
any steps taken by that licence holder towards remedying the consequences of the contravention of the requirement mentioned in paragraph (b)(i) and, where relevant, paragraph (b)(ii).

A penalty imposed on a licence holder under paragraph 9 or 10 for a contravention may not consist of or include a fixed amount exceeding 10% of the licence holder's qualifying turnover for the qualifying period.
A licence holder's qualifying turnover is the licence holder's turnover from its provision of air traffic services.

The qualifying period is the last regulatory year ending on or before the day on which the notice proposing the penalty is given under paragraph 11(1) (“the notice day”), except in the cases described in sub-paragraph (4).
Those cases are—
where a licence holder was not authorised to provide air traffic services in respect of a managed area throughout the last regulatory year that ends on or before the notice day;
where there is no regulatory year or the last regulatory year ended more than 12 months before the notice day;
where a licence holder has not provided the CAA with accounts prepared in accordance with the licence for the last regulatory year that ends on or before the notice day.
In those cases—

if the licence holder was authorised to provide air traffic services in respect of a managed area on the notice day, the qualifying period is the year ending with the notice day (or, if shorter, the period ending with the notice day during which the licence holder was authorised to provide such services in respect of such an area);

otherwise, the qualifying period is the year ending with the last day before the notice day on which the licence holder was authorised to provide air traffic services in respect of a managed area (or, if shorter, the period ending with the last day before the notice day during which the licence holder was authorised to provide such services in respect of such an area).

A licence holder's qualifying turnover for a qualifying period is to be taken to be the qualifying turnover for that period as reported in accounts that the licence holder is required to prepare by a licence condition, unless regulations under sub-paragraph (7) provide otherwise.
The Secretary of State may by regulations—
amend or otherwise modify the definition of qualifying turnover;
make provision about how a licence holder's qualifying turnover for a qualifying period is to be calculated.
The regulations may in particular—
make provision about cases in which turnover is or is not to be treated as qualifying turnover for a qualifying period;
provide that a licence holder's qualifying turnover for a qualifying period is to be taken to be the qualifying turnover reported in accounts specified or described in the regulations;
provide that a licence holder's qualifying turnover is to be calculated entirely or partly using accounting rules specified or described in the regulations.
In this paragraph “
”, in relation to a licence holder, means a year for which the licence holder was required to prepare accounts by a licence condition for air traffic services provided in respect of a managed area.
In relation to a penalty under paragraph 9 or 10, a daily amount is an amount payable where the contravention in respect of which the penalty is imposed continues after it is imposed.

A penalty under paragraph 9 may not consist of or include a daily amount unless that contravention has been continuous since the end of the representation period for the contravention notice in which the contravention was specified.
A daily amount must not exceed 0.1% of the licence holder's qualifying turnover for the qualifying period.
A daily amount is payable in respect of each day in a period specified by the CAA in the notice under paragraph 12 stating that it has imposed the penalty.
A specified period during which daily amounts accumulate must be the period that the CAA considers appropriate, subject to sub-paragraphs (6) and (7).
The period must begin after the day on which the CAA gives the notice under paragraph 12.
The period must end before—
the day on which the contravention specified in the notice under paragraph 12 ceases, or
if more than one contravention is specified in that notice, the day on which the last of those contraventions ceases.
In this paragraph “
” and “
” have the same meaning as in paragraph 14.

Emphasis.Addition: Use of powers under Competition Act 1998

Text.Addition: Before exercising a power listed in sub-paragraph (3), the CAA must consider whether it would be more appropriate to proceed under the Competition Act 1998.
The CAA must not exercise such a power to the extent that it considers it would be more appropriate to proceed under that Act.
Those powers are—
the power to give a contravention notice under paragraph 1;
the power to give an enforcement order under paragraph 3;
the power to give and confirm an urgent enforcement order under paragraphs 5 and 6;
the power to impose penalties under paragraphs 9 and 10.

Emphasis.Addition: Appeals against enforcement orders and urgent enforcement orders

Text.Addition: A licence holder may appeal to the Competition Appeal Tribunal (referred to in this Schedule as “
”) against—
an enforcement order given to the licence holder, or
an urgent enforcement order given to the licence holder that has been confirmed.
The appeal may be against one or more of the following—
the decision to give the order or, in the case of an urgent enforcement order, to confirm the order;
the decision as to the steps specified in the order;
the decision as to the period allowed for taking those steps.
The making of an appeal under this paragraph against an enforcement order suspends the effect of the order until the appeal is decided or withdrawn, unless the Tribunal orders otherwise.
The making of an appeal under this paragraph against an urgent enforcement order does not suspend the effect of the order, unless the Tribunal orders otherwise.

Emphasis.Addition: Appeals against modifications or revocations of existing orders

Text.Addition: A person may appeal to the Tribunal against—
a decision to modify or revoke an enforcement order, or
a decision to modify or revoke an urgent enforcement order that has been confirmed.
An appeal under this paragraph may be made only by a person—
who is not the person to whom the order was given, but
who appears to the Tribunal to have sufficient interest in the decision.

The making of an appeal under this paragraph against a modification or revocation of an order suspends the modification or revocation until the appeal is decided or withdrawn, unless the Tribunal orders otherwise.
A licence holder may appeal to the Tribunal against a penalty imposed on the licence holder under paragraph 9 or 10.
The appeal may be against one or more of the following—
the decision to impose the penalty;
the decision as to the amount of the penalty;
in the case of a penalty calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount, the decision as to the period during which the daily amounts accumulate;
the decision as to the period allowed for payment of the penalty.
Where a licence holder appeals under this paragraph against a penalty, the CAA may not require the licence holder to pay the penalty until the appeal is decided or withdrawn.
The Tribunal may allow an appeal under paragraph 17, 18 or 19 only to the extent that it is satisfied that the decision appealed against was wrong on one or more of the following grounds—
that the decision was based on an error of fact;
that the decision was wrong in law;
that an error was made in the exercise of a discretion.
It may—
confirm or set aside the order, modification, revocation or penalty;
give the CAA any directions it considers appropriate, including directions about the time within which the CAA must act.
It may not direct the CAA to do anything that the CAA would not have the power to do apart from the direction.
When deciding an appeal under paragraph 17, 18 or 19 (including giving directions) the Tribunal must have regard to the matters in respect of which duties are imposed on the CAA by section 2.
An appeal lies to the appropriate court on a point of law arising from a decision of the Tribunal under paragraph 20, including a direction.
An appeal under this paragraph may be brought by a party to the proceedings before the Tribunal.
An appeal may not be brought without the permission of—
the Tribunal, or
the appropriate court.
“The appropriate court”—
in the case of an appeal from proceedings in England and Wales or Northern Ireland, means the Court of Appeal;
in the case of an appeal from proceedings in Scotland, means the Court of Session.

References in this Schedule to remedying the consequences of a contravention of a Chapter 1 requirement, or a requirement of an enforcement order or an urgent enforcement order, include paying an amount to a person—
by way of compensation for loss or damage suffered by the person, or
in respect of annoyance, inconvenience or anxiety suffered by the person.
The CAA may by notice require a person to provide—
information, or
a document that is in the person's custody or under the person's control.
In this Schedule “
” means anything in which information is recorded.
The CAA may give a notice under this paragraph only in respect of information or documents that it reasonably requires for the purpose of carrying out its functions under section 34 or Schedule B1.
The notice may require the information or document to be provided—
at a time and place specified in the notice;
in a form and manner specified in the notice.

The notice may not require a person to provide information or documents that the person could not be compelled to provide in evidence in civil proceedings before the High Court or, in Scotland, the Court of Session.
If a person fails to comply with a notice under paragraph 1 without reasonable excuse, the CAA may do either or both of the following—
impose a penalty on the person;
enforce the duty to comply with the notice in civil proceedings for an injunction or, in Scotland, for specific performance of a statutory duty under section 45 of the Court of Session Act 1988.
The amount of the penalty must be the amount that the CAA determines to be—
appropriate, and
proportionate to the failure in respect of which it is imposed.
A penalty may consist of either or both of the following—
a fixed amount;
an amount payable in respect of each day in a period specified by the CAA (a “daily amount”).
A fixed amount must not exceed £2,000,000.
A daily amount must not exceed £100,000.
A specified period during which daily amounts accumulate must be the period that the CAA considers appropriate, subject to sub-paragraphs (7) and (8).
The period must begin after the day on which the CAA gives the notice under paragraph 6 stating that it has imposed the penalty.
The period must end before the day on which the person provides the information or documents specified in the notice under paragraph 1.
The Secretary of State may by regulations replace the amount for the time being specified in sub-paragraph (4) or (5).

The CAA may impose a penalty of a fixed amount on a person where it is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the person, in giving information to the CAA, has committed an offence under section 101 (making of false statements etc).

Where a penalty is imposed on a person under this paragraph by the CAA, that person may not at any time be convicted of the offence under section 101 in respect of the act or omission giving rise to the penalty.
The amount of a penalty imposed on a person under this paragraph must be the amount that the CAA determines to be—
appropriate, and
proportionate to the action in respect of which it is imposed,
but subject to a maximum of £2,000,000.
The CAA may impose a penalty of a fixed amount on a person if the person intentionally alters, suppresses or destroys a document that the person is required to produce by a notice under paragraph 1.
The reference in sub-paragraph (1) to suppressing a document includes a reference to destroying the means of reproducing information recorded otherwise than in a legible format.
The amount of a penalty imposed on a person under this paragraph must be the amount that the CAA determines to be—
appropriate, and
proportionate to the action in respect of which it is imposed,
but subject to a maximum of £2,000,000.
Before imposing a penalty on a person under paragraph 2, 3 or 4, the CAA must—
give the person a notice about the proposed penalty;
publish the notice as soon as practicable;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (4);
consider any representations made about the proposed penalty in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).
The notice under sub-paragraph (1) must—
state that the CAA proposes to impose a penalty;
state the proposed amount of the penalty;
give the CAA's reasons for imposing the penalty.
In the case of a penalty under paragraph 2 calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount, the notice under sub-paragraph (1) must specify—
the day on which daily amounts would begin to accumulate;
the day on which, or the circumstances in which, they would cease to accumulate.
The persons are—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
The period specified in the notice under sub-paragraph (1) for making representations must be a period of not less than 21 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given to the person.
Before varying the proposed amount of a penalty, the CAA must—
give the person on whom the penalty is to be imposed a notice about the proposed variation;
publish the notice as soon as practicable;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (4);
consider any representations made about the proposed variation in the period specified in the notice (and not withdrawn).

In the case of a penalty under paragraph 2 calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount, the reference in sub-paragraph (6) to varying the proposed amount of the penalty includes a reference to—
varying the day on which daily amounts would begin to accumulate, and
varying the day on which, or circumstances in which, they would cease to accumulate.
The notice under sub-paragraph (6) must—
specify the proposed variation;
give the CAA's reasons for the proposed variation.
The period specified in the notice under sub-paragraph (6) for making representations must be a period of not less than 21 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given to the person.
The CAA may withdraw a notice under sub-paragraph (1) or (6) at any time by giving notice to the person on whom it is proposed to impose the penalty.
As soon as practicable after giving a notice under sub-paragraph (10), the CAA must—
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (4).
As soon as practicable after imposing a penalty on a person under paragraph 2, 3 or 4, the CAA must—
give a notice to the person on whom the penalty is imposed;
publish the notice;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (4).
The notice must—
state that the CAA has imposed the penalty;
state the amount of the penalty;
give the CAA's reasons for imposing the penalty;
specify a reasonable period within which the penalty must be paid or reasonable periods within which different portions of the penalty must be paid.
In the case of a penalty under paragraph 2 calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount, the notice must specify—
the day on which the daily amounts begin to accumulate;
the day on which, or circumstances in which, they cease to accumulate.
The persons are—
any owners or operators of aircraft, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
any owners or managers of aerodromes, or any bodies representing them, that the CAA considers appropriate;
the Secretary of State.
As soon as practicable after daily amounts cease to accumulate, the CAA must—
give a notice to the person on whom the penalty was imposed confirming the day on which they ceased to accumulate;
send a copy of the notice to the persons listed in sub-paragraph (4).
A person may appeal to the Competition Appeal Tribunal against a penalty imposed on the person under paragraph 2, 3 or 4.
The appeal may be against one or more of the following—
a decision to impose a penalty;
a decision as to the amount of the penalty;
in the case of a penalty calculated entirely or partly by reference to a daily amount, a decision as to the period during which daily amounts accumulate;
a decision as to the period allowed for payment of the penalty.
Where a person appeals under this paragraph against a penalty, the CAA may not require the person to pay the penalty until the appeal is decided or withdrawn.

In any appeal where the commission of an offence under section 101 is an issue requiring determination, the CAA must prove that offence according to the same burden and standard of proof as in a criminal prosecution.
The Competition Appeal Tribunal may allow an appeal under paragraph 7 only to the extent that it is satisfied that the decision appealed against was wrong on one or more of the following grounds—
that the decision was based on an error of fact;
that the decision was wrong in law;
that an error was made in the exercise of a discretion.
It may—
confirm or set aside the penalty;
give the CAA any directions that it considers appropriate, including directions about the time within which the CAA must act.
It may not direct the CAA to do anything that the CAA would not have the power to do apart from the direction.

When deciding an appeal under paragraph 7 (including giving directions), the Competition Appeal Tribunal must have regard to the matters in respect of which duties are imposed on the CAA by section 2.
An appeal lies to the appropriate court on a point of law arising from a decision of the Competition Appeal Tribunal under paragraph 8, including a direction.
An appeal under this paragraph may be brought by a party to the proceedings before the Competition Appeal Tribunal.
An appeal may not be brought under this paragraph without the permission of—
the Competition Appeal Tribunal, or
the appropriate court.
“The appropriate court”—
in the case of an appeal from proceedings in England and Wales or Northern Ireland, means the Court of Appeal;
in the case of an appeal from proceedings in Scotland, means the Court of Session.

TitleBlock.Title: Air traffic administration orders: general

P1para.Text: This Part of this Schedule applies if an air traffic administration order is made.

Pblock.Title: General application of provisions of 1986 Act

P1para.Text: Sections 11 to 23 and 27 of the 1986 Act (which relate to administration orders under Part II of that Act) apply with the modifications specified in this Part of this Schedule.
In those sections as applied by this Part of this Schedule—

P3para.Text: references to an administration order are to an air traffic administration order, and
references to an administrator are to an air traffic administrator.

P1para.Text: In section 11 of the 1986 Act (effect of order) as applied by this Part of this Schedule—

P3para.Text: the requirement in subsection (1)(a) that any petition for the winding up of the company shall be dismissed does not prejudice the air traffic administration order if it is made by virtue of section 27 above,
the reference in subsection (3)(d) to proceedings includes a reference to any proceedings under or for the purposes of section 20 above, and
subsection (3)(d) has effect as if after “its property” there were inserted “ , and no right of re-entry or forfeiture may be enforced against the company in respect of any land, ”.

P1para.Text: In section 13 of the 1986 Act (appointment of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule for subsection (3) substitute—

P2para.Text: An application for an order under subsection (2) may be made—

P3para.Text: by the Secretary of State,
by the CAA with the Secretary of State’s consent,
by any continuing air traffic administrator of the company, or
where there is no such air traffic administrator, by the company, the directors or any creditor or creditors of the company.

Pblock.Title: General powers of air traffic administrator

P2para.Text: Section 14 of the 1986 Act (general powers of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
In subsection (1)(b) the reference to the powers specified in Schedule 1 to the 1986 Act includes a reference to a power to act on behalf of the company—

P3para.Text: for the purposes of this Part, or
for the purposes of the exercise or performance of any power or duty which is conferred or imposed on the company by virtue of its holding a licence.

P2para.Text: In subsection (4) the reference to a power conferred by the company’s articles of association includes a reference to a power conferred by virtue of the company’s holding a licence.

Pblock.Title: Power to deal with charged property

P2para.Text: Section 15 of the 1986 Act (power to deal with charged property) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
In subsection (2) for “the purpose or one or more of the purposes specified in the administration order” substitute “ one or both of the purposes of the administration order ”.

In subsection (5)(b) for “in the open market by a willing vendor” substitute “ for the best price which is reasonably available on a sale which is consistent with the purposes of the air traffic administration order ”.
Section 17 of the 1986 Act (duties of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
For subsection (2) substitute—

Subject to any directions of the court, it shall be the duty of the air traffic administrator to manage the affairs, business and property of the company in accordance with proposals under section 23 as they are revised from time to time.
In subsection (3) omit paragraph (a).
Section 18 of the 1986 Act (discharge and variation of administration order) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
For subsections (1) and (2) substitute—
An application for an air traffic administration order to be discharged may be made—

P3para.Text: by the air traffic administrator, on the ground that the purposes of the order have been achieved; or
by the Secretary of State or (with his consent) by the CAA, on the ground that it is no longer necessary that those purposes are achieved.

P2para.Text: In subsection (3) omit the words “or vary”.
In subsection (4)—

P3para.Text: omit the words “or varied” and “or variation”, and
after “to the registrar of companies” insert “ , to the CAA and to the Secretary of State ”.

P1para.Text: In section 21(2) of the 1986 Act (notice of order to be given by administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule after “to the registrar of companies” insert “ , to the CAA, to the Secretary of State ”.
In section 23 of the 1986 Act (statement of proposals) as applied by this Part of this Schedule for subsections (1) and (2) substitute—

P2para.Text: Where an air traffic administration order has been made, the air traffic administrator shall, within 3 months (or such longer period as the court may allow) after the making of the order, send a statement of his proposals for achieving the purposes of the order—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA,
to all creditors of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), and
to the registrar of companies.

P2para.Text: The air traffic administrator may from time to time revise those proposals.
If the air traffic administrator proposes to make revisions which appear to him to be substantial, he shall before making them send a statement of the proposed revisions—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA,
to all creditors of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), and
to the registrar of companies.

P2para.Text: The air traffic administrator shall give a copy of any statement under subsection (1) or (2A) to all members of the company before the end of the period described in subsection (1) or, as the case may be, before making the revisions.
The requirement in subsection (2B) is satisfied if the administrator—

P3para.Text: sends a copy of the statement to all members of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), or
publishes in the prescribed manner a notice stating an address to which members should write for copies of the statement to be sent to them free of charge.

P2para.Text: Section 27 of the 1986 Act (protection of interests of creditors and members) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
After subsection (1) insert—

If a creditor or member of the company makes an application under subsection (1), the court shall give notice of the application to the Secretary of State, who shall be entitled to be heard by the court in connection with the application.

At any time when an air traffic administration order is in force the Secretary of State or (with his consent) the CAA may apply to the court by petition for an order under this section on one or both of the following grounds.

The first ground is that the air traffic administrator has exercised or is exercising or proposing to exercise his powers in relation to the company in a manner which will not best ensure the achievement of the purposes of the order.
The second ground is that he has exercised or is exercising or proposing to exercise his powers in relation to the company in a manner which involves a contravention of—

P3para.Text: a condition of the licence granted under Chapter I of Part I of the Transport Act 2000, or
a duty imposed by section 8(1) of that Act, or
any other requirement imposed on the company by virtue of its holding the licence.

P2para.Text: Omit subsection (3).
In subsection (4) omit the words “Subject as above”.
After that subsection insert—

Provision may be made by virtue of subsection (4)(d) that the air traffic administration order is to be discharged from such date as may be specified in the order unless, before that date, such measures are taken as the court thinks fit for the purpose of protecting the interests of creditors.
For subsection (6) substitute—

Where an air traffic administration order is discharged, the air traffic administrator shall within 14 days after the date on which the discharge takes effect send a copy of the order under this section—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA, and
to the registrar of companies;

P2para.Text: and if, without reasonable excuse, the air traffic administrator fails to comply with this subsection, he is liable to a fine and, for continued contravention, to a daily default fine.

References in the 1986 Act (except in sections 8 to 10 and 24 to 26), or in any other enactment passed before the day on which this Act is passed, to an administration order under Part II of that Act, to an application for such an order and to an administrator include references (respectively) to an air traffic administration order, to an application for an air traffic administration order and to an air traffic administrator.

References in the 1986 Act, or in any other enactment passed before the day on which this Act is passed, to an enactment contained in Part II of that Act include references to that enactment as applied by section 30 above or Part I of this Schedule.
But—

P3para.Text: sub-paragraph (1) applies in relation to a reference in an enactment contained in Part II of the 1986 Act only so far as necessary for the purposes of the operation of the provisions of that Part as so applied;
sub-paragraphs (1) and (2) apply subject to Part I of this Schedule.

P1para.Text: The provisions of this Schedule are without prejudice to the power conferred by section 411 of the 1986 Act (company insolvency rules) as modified by paragraph 13(1) and (2).

P2para.Text: In this Schedule “the 1986 Act” means the Insolvency Act 1986.
For the purposes of this Schedule and any modification of the 1986 Act made by this Schedule—

P3para.Text: an air traffic administration order is an order made under section 27 or 28 above;
an air traffic administrator is a person appointed by the court to achieve the purposes of an air traffic administration order;
the CAA is the Civil Aviation Authority.

TitleBlock.Title: Air traffic administration orders: schemes

P1para.Text: This Schedule applies if—

P3para.Text: the court has made an air traffic administration order in relation to a licence company (the existing licence company), and
it is proposed that on and after the appointed day another company (the new licence company) should carry out licensed activities in respect of all or part of a licensed area.

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Schedule—

P3para.Text: an air traffic administration order is an order made under section 27 or 28;
an air traffic administrator is a person appointed by the court to achieve the purposes of an air traffic administration order;
the court is the court which (but for section 27) would have jurisdiction to wind up the existing licence company;
references to the existing licence company and the new licence company must be construed in accordance with paragraph 1;
references to a licence company are to be construed in accordance with section 26;
other licence companies are licence companies, other than the existing licence company and the new licence company;
licensed activities are activities which the licence concerned authorises the existing licence company to carry out;
a licensed area is an area in respect of which the licence concerned authorises the existing licence company to provide air traffic services;
the appointed day is a day which falls before the discharge of the air traffic administration order takes effect and which is appointed by the court for the purposes of this Schedule.

P2para.Text: The existing licence company, acting with the consent of the new licence company and, in relation to the matters affecting them, of any other licence companies, may make a scheme designed to secure that the new licence company carries out licensed activities in respect of all or part of the licensed area.
No scheme takes effect unless it is approved by the Secretary of State after consulting the CAA.
If a scheme is submitted to the Secretary of State for approval he may modify the scheme before approving it.
But no modification may be made unless the following consent—

P3para.Text: the new licence company,
the existing licence company, and
in relation to the matters affecting them, any other licence companies.

P2para.Text: A scheme comes into force on the appointed day.

At any time after a scheme has come into force, if he thinks it appropriate the Secretary of State may by order provide that the scheme is to be taken for all purposes to have come into force with the modifications specified in the order.
But the Secretary of State may not make an order under sub-paragraph (6) unless the following consent—

P3para.Text: the existing licence company,
the new licence company, and
in relation to the provisions of the order which affect them, any other licence companies.

P2para.Text: An order under sub-paragraph (6)—

P3para.Text: may make, with effect from the coming into force of the scheme to which it relates, any such provision as could have been made by the scheme, and
in connection with giving effect to that provision from that time, may make such supplementary, consequential and transitional provision as the Secretary of State thinks appropriate.

P2para.Text: A scheme may provide for a licence held by the existing licence company to have effect, with such modifications as the scheme may specify, as if the licence had been granted to the new licence company.
If different schemes are made in relation to different parts of the licensed area—

P3para.Text: each scheme has effect as if there were a separate licence in respect of each part, and
each licence has effect as if it had been granted to the company which is the new licence company under the scheme concerned.

P1para.Text: A scheme may provide for the transfer of property, rights and liabilities from the existing licence company to the new licence company.

P2para.Text: In determining whether and in what manner to exercise the powers under paragraph 3 to approve and modify a scheme, the Secretary of State must have regard to the need to ensure that a scheme allocates property, rights and liabilities to the new licence company in such manner as appears to the Secretary of State to be appropriate.
In deciding what is appropriate the Secretary of State must take into account the licensed activities which will be carried out on or after the appointed day by any of—

P3para.Text: the new licence company,
the existing licence company, and
any other licence companies.

P2para.Text: When a scheme comes into force, it has effect without more so as to transfer to the new licence company the property, rights and liabilities to which the scheme relates.
A scheme may divide the property, rights or liabilities of the existing licence company and in connection with that division may—

P3para.Text: create for the existing licence company, the new licence company or any other licence companies an interest in or right over any property to which the scheme relates;
create new rights and liabilities as between any two or more of those companies with respect to the subject-matter of the scheme;

in connection with any provision made by virtue of paragraph (a) or (b), make incidental provision as to the interests, rights and liabilities of other persons with respect to the subject-matter of the scheme.

P2para.Text: A scheme may impose duties on the existing licence company, the new licence company and any other licence company to take all such steps as may be necessary to secure that—

P3para.Text: any interest, right or liability created by virtue of paragraph (a) or (b) of sub-paragraph (2), and
any incidental provision made by virtue of paragraph (c) of that sub-paragraph,

P2para.Text: has effect.

A scheme may require the new licence company and any other licence companies to provide consideration in respect of the transfer or creation of property, rights and liabilities by means of the scheme.

A requirement imposed under sub-paragraph (4) is enforceable in the same way as if the property, rights and liabilities had been created or transferred, and (if the case so requires) had been capable of being created or transferred, by agreement between the parties.
The property, rights and liabilities of the existing licence company which may be transferred in accordance with a scheme include—

P3para.Text: property, rights and liabilities which the existing licence company would not otherwise be capable of transferring or assigning;
property, rights and liabilities to which the existing licence company may become entitled or subject after the making of the scheme and before the appointed day;
property situated anywhere in the United Kingdom or elsewhere;
rights and liabilities under enactments;
rights and liabilities under the law of any part of the United Kingdom or of any country or territory outside the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: If a scheme makes a person entitled to possession of a document, the provision that may be made by virtue of sub-paragraph (2)(b) includes—

P3para.Text: provision for treating that person as having given another person an acknowledgement in writing of the right of that other person to the production of the document and to delivery of copies of it,
provision applying section 64 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (production and safe custody of documents) to that acknowledgement,

provision that, where a scheme transfers any interest in land or other property situated in Scotland, subsections (1) and (2) of section 16 of the Land Registration (Scotland) Act 1979 (omission of certain clauses in deeds) are to have effect in relation to the transfer as if the transfer had been effected by deed and as if from each of those subsections the words “unless specially qualified” had been omitted, and
provision applying section 9 of the Conveyancing Act 1881 (which is the equivalent in Northern Ireland to section 64 of the Law of Property Act 1925) to that acknowledgement.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (9) applies if a transfer authorised by sub-paragraph (6)(a) would (were it not so authorised)—

P3para.Text: give rise to a contravention or liability by reason of a provision relating to the terms on which the existing licence company is entitled or subject to the property, right or liability transferred, or
give rise to an interference with any interest or right by reason of such a provision.

P2para.Text: In such a case the transfer does not give rise to such a contravention, liability or interference.
The provision referred to in sub-paragraph (8) may arise under an enactment or agreement or otherwise.

A scheme may impose duties on the existing licence company and on the new licence company to take all such steps as may be necessary to secure that the vesting in the new licence company, by virtue of the scheme, of any foreign property, right or liability is effective under the relevant foreign law.

A scheme may require the existing licence company to comply with any directions given by the new licence company in performing any duty imposed on the existing licence company by virtue of a provision included in the scheme under sub-paragraph (1).

A scheme may provide that, until the vesting of any foreign property, right or liability of the existing licence company in the new licence company is effective under the relevant foreign law, it is the duty of the existing licence company—

P3para.Text: to hold that property or right for the benefit of the new licence company, or
to discharge that liability on behalf of the new licence company.

P2para.Text: A scheme may provide that in specified cases foreign property, rights or liabilities acquired or incurred by an existing licence company after the scheme comes into force are immediately to become property, rights or liabilities of the new licence company; and in relation to such property, rights or liabilities the scheme may make provision equivalent to that in sub-paragraphs (1) to (3).

Nothing in any provision included in a scheme by virtue of this paragraph affects the law of any part of the United Kingdom as it applies to the vesting of any foreign property, right or liability in the new licence company by virtue of the scheme.

References in this paragraph to any foreign property, right or liability are references to any property, right or liability as respects which any issue arising in any proceedings would have to be determined (in accordance with the rules of private international law) by reference to the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.
Any expenses incurred by an existing licence company in consequence of any provision included in a scheme by virtue of this paragraph must be met by the new licence company.

Duties imposed on an existing licence company or a new licence company by virtue of this paragraph are enforceable in the same way as if they were imposed by a contract between the existing licence company and the new licence company.
A scheme may contain supplementary, consequential and transitional provision for the purposes of, or in connection with, any provision of the scheme.
In particular a scheme may provide—

P3para.Text: that for purposes connected with any transfers made in accordance with the scheme (including the transfer of rights and liabilities under an enactment) the new licence company is to be treated as the same person in law as the existing licence company;

that (so far as may be necessary for the purposes of or in connection with any such transfers) agreements made, transactions effected and other things done by or in relation to the existing licence company are to be treated as made, effected or done by or in relation to the new licence company;
