that (so far as may be necessary for the purposes of or in connection with any such transfers) references in any agreement (whether or not in writing) or in any document to, or to any officer of, the existing licence company are to have effect with such modifications as the scheme may specify;
that proceedings commenced by or against the existing licence company are to be continued by or against the new licence company;

that contracts of employment with the existing licence company are not to terminate and that periods of employment with the existing licence company are to count for all purposes as periods of employment with the new licence company;

that disputes about the effect of the scheme between the existing licence company and the new licence company, between either of them and any other licence company or between different companies which are other licence companies are to be referred to such arbitration as may be specified in or determined under the scheme;
that determinations on such arbitrations are conclusive for all purposes;

that certificates given jointly by two or more of the licence companies mentioned in paragraph (f) as to the effect of the scheme as between the licence companies giving the certificates are conclusive for all purposes.

P2para.Text: The new licence company, the existing licence company and any other licence companies which are likely to be affected by a scheme must provide the Secretary of State with all such information and other assistance as the Secretary of State may reasonably require for the purposes of, or in connection with, the exercise of any power conferred by paragraph 3.

If a company without reasonable excuse fails to do anything required of it by sub-paragraph (1) it is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Pblock.Title: Effect of air traffic administration order

P1para.Text: While an air traffic administration order is in force in relation to an existing licence company anything which the company is permitted or required to do—

P3para.Text: by paragraph 3 or 10, or
in consequence of any provision of a scheme,

P1para.Text: is effective only if it is done on the company’s behalf by its air traffic administrator.

TitleBlock.Title: Air traffic administration orders: Northern Ireland

P1para.Text: In their application to a licence company formed and registered under the Companies Act 2006 in Northern Ireland, sections 26 to 32 and Schedules 1 and 2 have effect with the modifications made by this Schedule.

P2para.Text: Section 26 is modified as follows.
In subsection (2) for “Part II of the 1986 Act” substitute “ Part III of the 1989 Order ”.
In subsection (5) for “Parts I to VII of the 1986 Act” substitute “ Parts II to VII of the 1989 Order ”.
In subsection (6)—

P3para.Text: for “the 1986 Act” substitute “ the 1989 Order ”, and
for “the Insolvency Act 1986” substitute “ the Insolvency (Northern Ireland) Order 1989 ”.

P2para.Text: Section 28 is modified as follows.
In subsection (3) for paragraph (a) substitute—

P3para.Text: the Secretary of State certifies that but for section 27 it would in his opinion be appropriate for the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Investment to petition for the company’s winding up under Article 104A of the 1989 Order (petition following inspectors’ report etc), and

P2para.Text: In subsection (3)(b) for “section 124A” substitute “ Article 104A ”.
In subsection (6) for “section 123 of the 1986 Act” substitute “ Article 103 of the 1989 Order ”.

P1para.Text: In section 29(5) for “the 1986 Act” substitute “ the 1989 Order ”.

P2para.Text: Section 30 is modified as follows.
In subsection (2) for “Section 9(4) and (5) of the 1986 Act” substitute “ Article 22(4) and (5) of the 1989 Order ”.
In subsection (3)—

P3para.Text: in paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d) for “subsection” substitute “ paragraph ”.

P2para.Text: In subsection (5)—

P3para.Text: for “section 411 of the 1986 Act” substitute “ Article 359 of the 1989 Order ”, and
for “Parts I to VII of that Act” substitute “ Parts II to VII of that Order ”.

P1para.Text: For Schedule 1 substitute—

TitleBlock.Title: Air traffic administration orders: general

P1para.Text: This Part of this Schedule applies if an air traffic administration order is made in Northern Ireland.

Pblock.Title: General application of provisions of 1989 Order

P1para.Text: Articles 24 to 35 and 39 of the 1989 Order (which relate to administration orders under Part III of that Order) apply with the modifications specified in this Part of this Schedule.
In those Articles as applied by this Part of this Schedule—

P3para.Text: references to an administration order are to an air traffic administration order, and
references to an administrator are to an air traffic administrator.

P1para.Text: In Article 24 of the 1989 Order (effect of order) as applied by this Part of this Schedule—

P3para.Text: the requirement in paragraph (1)(a) that any petition for the winding up of the company shall be dismissed does not prejudice the air traffic administration order if it is made by virtue of section 27 above,
the reference in paragraph (3)(d) to proceedings includes a reference to any proceedings under or for the purposes of section 20 above, and
paragraph (3)(d) has effect as if after “its property” there were inserted “, and no right of re-entry or forfeiture may be enforced against the company in respect of any land,”.

P1para.Text: In Article 26 of the 1989 Order (appointment of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule for paragraph (3) substitute—

P2para.Text: An application for an order under paragraph (2) may be made—

P3para.Text: by the Secretary of State,
by the CAA with the Secretary of State’s consent,
by any continuing air traffic administrator of the company, or
where there is no such air traffic administrator, by the company, the directors or any creditor or creditors of the company. ”

Pblock.Title: General powers of air traffic administrator

P2para.Text: Article 27 of the 1989 Order (general powers of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
In paragraph (1)(b) the reference to the powers specified in Schedule 1 to the 1989 Order includes a reference to a power to act on behalf of the company—

P3para.Text: for the purposes of this Part, or
for the purposes of the exercise or performance of any power or duty which is conferred or imposed on the company by virtue of its holding a licence.

P2para.Text: In paragraph (4) the reference to a power conferred by the company’s articles of association includes a reference to a power conferred by virtue of the company’s holding a licence.

Pblock.Title: Power to deal with charged property

P2para.Text: Article 28 of the 1989 Order (power to deal with charged property) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
In paragraph (2) for “the purpose or one or more of the purposes specified in the administration order” substitute “one or both of the purposes of the administration order”.

In paragraph (5)(b) for “in the open market by a willing vendor” substitute “for the best price which is reasonably available on a sale which is consistent with the purposes of the air traffic administration order”.
Article 29 of the 1989 Order (duties of administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
For paragraph (2) substitute—

Subject to any directions of the High Court, it shall be the duty of the air traffic administrator to manage the affairs, business and property of the company in accordance with proposals under Article 35 as they are revised from time to time. ”
In paragraph (3) omit sub-paragraph (a).
Article 30 of the 1989 Order (discharge and variation of administration order) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
For paragraphs (1) and (2) substitute—
An application for an air traffic administration order to be discharged may be made—

P3para.Text: by the air traffic administrator, on the ground that the purposes of the order have been achieved; or
by the Secretary of State or (with his consent) by the CAA, on the ground that it is no longer necessary that those purposes are achieved. ”

P2para.Text: In paragraph (3) omit the words “or vary”.
In paragraph (4)—

P3para.Text: omit the words “or varied” and “or variation”, and
after “to the registrar” insert “, to the CAA and to the Secretary of State”.

P1para.Text: In Article 33(2) of the 1989 Order (notice of order to be given by administrator) as applied by this Part of this Schedule after “to the registrar” insert “,to the CAA,to the Secretary of State”.
In Article 35 of the 1989 Order (statement of proposals) as applied by this Part of this Schedule for paragraphs (1) and (2) substitute—

P2para.Text: Where an air traffic administration order has been made, the air traffic administrator shall, within 3 months (or such longer period as the High Court may allow) after the making of the order, send a statement of his proposals for achieving the purposes of the order—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA,
to all creditors of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), and
to the registrar.

P2para.Text: The air traffic administrator may from time to time revise those proposals.
If the air traffic administrator proposes to make revisions which appear to him to be substantial, he shall before making them send a statement of the proposed revisions—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA,
to all creditors of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), and
to the registrar.

P2para.Text: The air traffic administrator shall give a copy of any statement under paragraph (1) or (2A) to all members of the company before the end of the period described in paragraph (1) or, as the case may be, before making the revisions.
The requirement in paragraph (2B) is satisfied if the administrator—

P3para.Text: sends a copy of the statement to all members of the company (so far as he is aware of their addresses), or
publishes in the prescribed manner a notice stating an address to which members should write for copies of the statement to be sent to them free of charge. ”

P2para.Text: Article 39 of the 1989 Order (protection of interests of creditors and members) as applied by this Part of this Schedule has effect as follows.
After paragraph (1) insert—

If a creditor or member of the company makes an application under paragraph (1), the court shall give notice of the application to the Secretary of State, who shall be entitled to be heard by the court in connection with the application.

At any time when an air traffic administration order is in force the Secretary of State or (with his consent) the CAA may apply to the court by petition for an order under this Article on one or both of the following grounds.

The first ground is that the air traffic administrator has exercised or is exercising or proposing to exercise his powers in relation to the company in a manner which will not best ensure the achievement of the purposes of the order.
The second ground is that he has exercised or is exercising or proposing to exercise his powers in relation to the company in a manner which involves a contravention of—

P3para.Text: a condition of the licence granted under Chapter I of Part I of the Transport Act 2000, or
a duty imposed by section 8(1) of that Act, or
any other requirement imposed on the company by virtue of its holding the licence. ”

P2para.Text: Omit paragraph (3).
In paragraph (4) omit the words “Subject to paragraph (3),”.
After that paragraph insert—

Provision may be made by virtue of paragraph (4)(d) that the air traffic administration order is to be discharged from such date as may be specified in the order unless, before that date, such measures are taken as the court thinks fit for the purpose of protecting the interests of creditors. ”
For paragraph (6) substitute—

Where an air traffic administration order is discharged, the air traffic administrator shall within 14 days after the date on which the discharge takes effect send a copy of the order under this Article—

P3para.Text: to the Secretary of State,
to the CAA, and
to the registrar;

P2para.Text: and if, without reasonable excuse, the air traffic administrator contravenes this paragraph, he shall be guilty of an offence and, for continued contravention, he shall be guilty of a continuing offence. ”

References in the 1989 Order (except in Articles 21 to 23 and 36 to 38), or in any other enactment passed before the day on which this Act is passed, to an administration order under Part III of that Order, to an application for such an order and to an administrator include references (respectively) to an air traffic administration order, to an application for an air traffic administration order and to an air traffic administrator.

References in the 1989 Order, or in any other enactment passed before the day on which this Act is passed, to an enactment contained in Part III of that Order include references to that enactment as applied by section 30 above or Part I of this Schedule.
But—

P3para.Text: sub-paragraph (1) applies in relation to a reference in an enactment contained in Part III of the 1989 Order only so far as necessary for the purposes of the operation of the provisions of that Part as so applied;
sub-paragraphs (1) and (2) apply subject to Part I of this Schedule.

P1para.Text: The provisions of this Schedule are without prejudice to the power conferred by Article 359 of the 1989 Order (insolvency rules) as modified by paragraph 13(1) and (2).

P2para.Text: In this Schedule “the 1989 Order” means the Insolvency (Northern Ireland) Order 1989.
For the purposes of this Schedule and any modification of the 1989 Order made by this Schedule—

P3para.Text: an air traffic administration order is an order made under section 27 or 28 above;
an air traffic administrator is a person appointed by the court to achieve the purposes of an air traffic administration order;
the CAA is the Civil Aviation Authority.

TitleBlock.Title: Licence holders: land

P1para.Text: The Civil Aviation Act 1982 shall be amended as follows.
After section 42 (acquisition of land by CAA) insert the following—

P1group.Title: Acquisition of land: air traffic services licence holders.

P2para.Text: A licence holder may be authorised by the Secretary of State to acquire land in Great Britain compulsorily for any purpose connected with the carrying out of the activities authorised by the licence.
Where a licence holder proposes to acquire, otherwise than by agreement, any land in Northern Ireland—

P3para.Text: which is required by the licence holder for any purpose connected with the carrying out of the activities authorised by the licence, or
as to which it can reasonably be foreseen that it will be so required,

P2para.Text: the licence holder may apply to the Secretary of State for an order vesting the land in it, and the Secretary of State shall have power to make such an order.
The Secretary of State shall not grant an authorisation under subsection (1) or an order under subsection (2) to a licence holder in respect of land which is owned by another licence holder who—

P3para.Text: is using it, or
will, in the opinion of the Secretary of State, use it at some time in the period of five years beginning with the date on which he receives the request for the authorisation or order.

P2para.Text: A reference in subsection (3) to use of land by a licence holder is a reference to use for a purpose connected with the carrying out of the activities authorised by the licence.
The following provisions of section 42 shall apply for the purposes of this section in relation to a licence holder as they apply for the purposes of that section in relation to the CAA—

subsection (3),

subsection (6).

TitleBlock.Title: Licence holders as statutory undertakers

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the provisions mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)—

P3para.Text: a licence holder carrying out activities authorised by its licence is to be taken to be a statutory undertaker;
its undertaking as licence holder is to be taken to be a statutory undertaking.

P2para.Text: The provisions are—

P3para.Text: the Acquisition of Land (Authorisation Procedure) (Scotland) Act 1947;
section 4 of the Requisitioned Land and War Works Act 1948;
the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949;
the Reserve and Auxiliary Forces (Protection of Civil Interests) Act 1951;
the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954;
section 39(6)(b) of the Opencast Coal Act 1958;
section 11 of the Land Compensation Act 1961;
section 18 of the Land Compensation (Scotland) Act 1963;
Schedule 3 to the Harbours Act 1964;

the New Towns (Scotland) Act 1968;

section 22 of the Sewerage (Scotland) Act 1968;
sections ... 296 and 611 of the Housing Act 1985.

P2para.Text: The provisions mentioned in sub-paragraph (2) apply in relation to—

P3para.Text: a licence holder carrying out activities authorised by its licence, and
any property which is owned by the licence holder,

P2para.Text: as they apply in relation to a railway company and its railway.
The provisions are—

P3para.Text: section 330 of the Public Health Act 1936 (power of certain undertakers in England and Wales to alter sewers);
section 333 of that Act (protection of certain undertakings in England and Wales from works executed under that Act);

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the Pipe-lines Act 1962—

P3para.Text: a licence holder carrying out activities authorised by its licence is to be taken to be a statutory undertaker;
its undertaking as licence holder is to be taken to be a statutory undertaking.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of section 13 of the 1962 Act, in relation to a licence holder operational land is land—

P3para.Text: which is used by the licence holder, or by a company associated with it, for the purpose of carrying out activities authorised by the licence, or
in which the licence holder, or a company associated with it, holds an interest for that purpose.

P2para.Text: If for the purposes of section 13 of the 1962 Act a question arises whether land is operational land in relation to a licence holder the question must be decided by the Secretary of State.

TitleBlock.Title: Transfer schemes

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 2 and 3 apply if the following two conditions are satisfied.
The first condition is that—

P3para.Text: provision is made by a transfer scheme for the transfer to a transferee of a specified part of a transferor’s undertaking, or
provision is made by a transfer scheme (or transfer schemes) for the transfer to different transferees of different specified parts of a transferor’s undertaking.

P2para.Text: The second condition is that any property, right or liability falls partly in one part of the undertaking and partly in another or others; and the parts of the undertaking are—

P3para.Text: the part (or each part) transferred, and
if a part is retained by the transferor, that part.

P2para.Text: In paragraphs 2 and 3 references to the parties are to—

P3para.Text: the transferee or transferees concerned, and
the transferor (if he retains part of the undertaking).

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 2 and 3 do not apply to rights or liabilities under a contract of employment.

If the nature of the property, right or liability permits, it must be apportioned in appropriate proportions between the parties; and each appropriate part must be taken to have been transferred to a transferee or retained by the transferor.
If an estate or interest in land is to be apportioned under sub-paragraph (1)—

P3para.Text: any rent payable under a lease in respect of the estate or interest, and
any rent charged on the estate or interest,

P2para.Text: must be apportioned so that an appropriate part of the rent is payable in respect of (or charged on) the appropriate part of the estate or interest.

Sub-paragraph (2) applies, with any necessary modifications, in relation to any feuduty payable in respect of an estate or interest in land in Scotland as it applies in relation to any rent charged on an estate or interest in land.

If the nature of the property, right or liability does not permit it to be apportioned as mentioned in paragraph 2(1), it must be taken to have been transferred to a transferee or retained by the transferor in accordance with the tests in sub-paragraphs (2) and (3).
In the case of an estate or interest in land the test is—

P3para.Text: which one of the parties has the greater (or greatest) need of the estate or interest for business purposes, or
if it is not possible to say that one of them has the greater (or greatest) need, which one of them is likely to make more (or the most) use of the land.

P2para.Text: In the case of any other property or any right or liability, the test is which one of the parties is likely—

P3para.Text: to make more (or the most) use of the property, or
to be more (or the most) affected by the right or liability.

P2para.Text: The tests in sub-paragraphs (2) and (3) must be applied at—

P3para.Text: the time when the transfer scheme comes into force (or schemes come into force), or
if there are two or more schemes and they come into force at different times, the later or latest of the times.

P2para.Text: The preceding provisions of this paragraph apply subject to any arrangements made by the parties as to the protection of the interests of any of them.
Paragraphs 5 to 7 apply if—

P3para.Text: provision is made by a transfer scheme for the transfer to a transferee of a specified part of a transferor’s undertaking, or
provision is made by a transfer scheme (or transfer schemes) for the transfer to different transferees of different specified parts of a transferor’s undertaking.

P2para.Text: It is immaterial whether or not the second condition set out in paragraph 1 is satisfied.
In paragraphs 5 to 7 references to the parties are to—

P3para.Text: the transferee or transferees concerned, and
the transferor (if he retains part of the undertaking).

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 5 to 7 do not apply to rights or liabilities under a contract of employment.

The parties must, so far as practicable, make any written agreement necessary or expedient to identify what is to be taken to have been transferred to whom and what (if anything) is to be taken to have been retained.
The duty under sub-paragraph (1) has effect before as well as after the coming into force of any transfer scheme concerned.
If the Secretary of State thinks it is unlikely that agreement will be reached on a matter where agreement is required under paragraph 5 he may serve a notice on the parties.
A notice may be served—

P3para.Text: whether or not representations are made by a party;
before or after the coming into force of any transfer scheme concerned.

P2para.Text: A notice may specify the terms of the agreement which the Secretary of State thinks the parties should have made under paragraph 5 in relation to the matter concerned.
If a notice is served under this paragraph the parties are to be treated as having made an agreement in the terms specified.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: an agreement made under paragraph 5, or
an agreement treated as made by paragraph 6,

P2para.Text: contains provision to the effect that any property, right or liability is to be taken to have been transferred to a transferee.
The property, right or liability is to be treated as having been transferred to the transferee by the scheme concerned (or, if there are two or more schemes, such of them as the agreement specifies).
Paragraphs 9 and 10 apply if—

P3para.Text: provision is made by a transfer scheme for the transfer to a transferee of a specified part of a transferor’s undertaking, or
provision is made by a transfer scheme (or transfer schemes) for the transfer to different transferees of different specified parts of a transferor’s undertaking.

P2para.Text: It is immaterial whether or not the second condition set out in paragraph 1 is satisfied.
In paragraphs 9 and 10 references to the parties are to—

P3para.Text: the transferee or transferees concerned, and
the transferor (if he retains part of the undertaking).

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 9 and 10 do not apply to rights or liabilities under a contract of employment.
Sub-paragraph (6) applies if at the time a transfer scheme comes into force a transferor or transferee under the scheme is—

P3para.Text: a company which is wholly owned by the Crown;
a company which is wholly owned by the CAA;
a company which is a wholly owned subsidiary of a company falling within paragraph (a) or (b).

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 9 and 10 cease to apply in relation to the scheme concerned at the time when the transferor or any one of the transferees under the scheme ceases to be a company which falls within any of paragraphs (a) to (c) of sub-paragraph (5).
The parties must, so far as practicable, make any written agreement and execute any other instrument necessary or expedient to—

P3para.Text: give to any party (as against another or others) any rights and safeguards needed for carrying out the party’s functions;
modify the division of the transferor’s undertaking in order to help the parties in carrying out their functions.

P2para.Text: An agreement or instrument under sub-paragraph (1) may provide—

P3para.Text: for the granting of leases and for the creation of other rights and liabilities over land (whether or not amounting in law to interests in land and whether or not involving the surrender of any existing interest or the creation of a new interest);
for the granting of indemnities in connection with the severance of leases and other matters;
for responsibility for registration of any matter in any statutory register.

P2para.Text: The duty under sub-paragraph (1) has effect before as well as after the coming into force of any transfer scheme concerned.
If the Secretary of State thinks it is unlikely that agreement will be reached on a matter where agreement is required under paragraph 9 he may serve a notice on the parties.
A notice may be served—

P3para.Text: whether or not representations are made by a party;
before or after the coming into force of any transfer scheme concerned.

P2para.Text: A notice may specify the terms of the agreement which the Secretary of State thinks the parties should have made under paragraph 9 in relation to the matter concerned.
If a notice is served under this paragraph the parties are to be treated as having made an agreement in the terms specified.

If a transfer scheme provides for property, rights or liabilities to be transferred from a transferor to a transferee, they may agree that such of the property, rights or liabilities as are specified in the agreement are to be transferred from the transferee to the transferor.

If one or more transfer schemes provide for different property, rights or liabilities to be transferred to different transferees, any transferee may agree with another that such of the property, rights or liabilities as are specified in the agreement are to be transferred from one to the other.
This paragraph does not apply to rights or liabilities under a contract of employment.
An agreement under this paragraph—

P3para.Text: must be in writing;
must be made before the end of the required period;
must be made with the Secretary of State’s approval.

P2para.Text: The required period is the period of 12 months starting with—

P3para.Text: the day on which the transfer scheme comes into force (or schemes come into force), or
if there are two or more schemes and they come into force on different days, the later or latest of the days.

P2para.Text: An agreement under this paragraph may provide for a transfer to take effect on a date specified in or determined in accordance with the agreement; but the agreement may provide that a transfer is not to take effect unless the circumstances are such as the agreement specifies.

When a transfer agreed under this paragraph takes effect the agreement has effect to transfer (in accordance with its provisions) the property, rights or liabilities concerned, subject to any enactment which provides for transactions to be registered in a statutory register.

This paragraph applies if on a transfer under a transfer scheme a transferor is entitled to retain possession of any document relating in part to the title to, or to the management of, any land or other property transferred to a transferee.
If the land or other property is situated in England and Wales—

P3para.Text: the transferor is to be treated as having given the transferee an acknowledgement in writing of the transferee’s right to production of the document and to delivery of copies of it, and

section 64 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (production and safe custody of documents) is to apply to the acknowledgement and is to apply on the basis that the acknowledgement does not contain an expression of contrary intention.

P2para.Text: If the land or other property is situated in Scotland, subsections (1) and (2) of section 16 of the Land Registration (Scotland) Act 1979 (omission of certain clauses in deeds) is to have effect in relation to the transfer as if the transfer had been effected by deed and as if from each of those subsections the words “unless specially qualified” were omitted.
If the land or other property is situated in Northern Ireland—

P3para.Text: the transferor is to be treated as having given the transferee an acknowledgement in writing of the transferee’s right to production of the document and to delivery of copies of it, and

section 9 of the Conveyancing Act 1881 (which corresponds to section 64 of the Law of Property Act 1925) is to apply to the acknowledgement and is to apply on the basis that the acknowledgement does not contain an expression of contrary intention.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if a transfer scheme provides for the transfer of foreign property, rights or liabilities from a transferor to a transferee.

The transferor and the transferee must take such steps as may be necessary to secure that the vesting of the property, rights or liabilities in the transferee is effective under the relevant foreign law; and the transferor must take the steps at such times as the transferee may specify in directions given to the transferor.
Until the vesting of the property, rights or liabilities in the transferee is effective under the relevant foreign law, the transferor must—

P3para.Text: hold the property or rights for the transferee’s benefit, or
discharge the liabilities on the transferee’s behalf.

P2para.Text: The transferor is to have all powers necessary for the performance of his duty under sub-paragraph (2), but the transferee must act on the transferor’s behalf (so far as possible) in the performance of that duty.

Nothing in sub-paragraphs (2) to (4) affects the law of the United Kingdom (or of any part of the United Kingdom) as it applies to the vesting of the property, rights or liabilities in the transferee by virtue of the transfer scheme.

References in this paragraph to foreign property, rights or liabilities are references to property, rights or liabilities as respects which any issue arising in any proceedings would be determined (in accordance with the rules of private international law) by reference to the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.
The transferee must meet any expenses incurred by the transferor in consequence of this paragraph.
Duties imposed on the transferor or the transferee by this paragraph are enforceable in the same way as if they were imposed by a contract between them.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: a transfer scheme provides for the transfer of property, rights or liabilities from a transferor to a transferee, and
a certificate falling within sub-paragraph (2) is made jointly by or on behalf of the parties.

P2para.Text: A certificate falls within this sub-paragraph if it certifies that any specified property, right or liability—

P3para.Text: was intended to be, and was, vested in the transferee by virtue of the transfer, and
has not been the subject of an agreement under paragraph 11.

P2para.Text: The certificate is to be conclusive evidence for all purposes of the facts it certifies.
The reference in sub-paragraph (2) to property includes a reference to an interest in or right over property.
Sub-paragraph (6) applies if—

P3para.Text: one of the parties requests the other to join in the preparation of a certificate, and
they fail to agree the terms of a certificate within the period of one month starting with the day of the request.

P2para.Text: The parties must—

P3para.Text: refer the matter to the Secretary of State, and
issue a certificate in such terms as may be specified in a direction given by him.

P2para.Text: The parties are the transferor and the transferee.
For the purposes of this paragraph a person is a party if—

P3para.Text: he is the transferor (or one of the transferors) under a transfer scheme and holds an interest in land immediately after the scheme comes into force, or
he is the transferee (or one of the transferees) under the scheme and an interest in land is transferred to him under the scheme.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this paragraph the relevant land is any land in which any party has an interest immediately after the scheme comes into force.

On the representation of any of the parties the Secretary of State may give to the parties a direction stating that sub-paragraph (4) is to apply to such of the relevant land as the direction specifies.
While the direction remains in force—

P3para.Text: no party may dispose of an interest in any of the specified land unless the Secretary of State consents;

if a party proposes to dispose of such an interest and the Secretary of State thinks it necessary or expedient to exercise any of the powers set out in sub-paragraph (5) for the protection of any other party, the Secretary of State may exercise any of those powers.

P2para.Text: The powers are—

P3para.Text: power to consent to the proposed disposal subject to compliance with such conditions as the Secretary of State may see fit to impose;
power to require a party to dispose of an interest in any of the specified land to such person and in such manner as may be specified in the requirement;
power to require a party to acquire another party’s interest in any of the specified land.

P2para.Text: In sub-paragraph (5)(b) and (c) references to an interest include (but are not limited to) references to the interest whose disposal is proposed.
A person who is not a party and who is dealing with a party (or with a person claiming under a party) in relation to land is not to be concerned to see or enquire—

P3para.Text: whether this paragraph applies (or has applied) in relation to any of the land;
whether a direction under this paragraph has been given in relation to any of the land;
whether this paragraph or any condition imposed or requirement made under it has been complied with in connection with the dealing or any other dealing concerning any of the land.

P2para.Text: No transaction between a person who is not a party (on the one hand) and a party or a person claiming under a party (on the other) is to be invalid by reason of any failure to comply with this paragraph or any condition imposed or requirement made under it.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: a transfer scheme provides for the transfer of property, rights or liabilities from a transferor to a transferee, and
immediately before the coming into force of the scheme the transferor was entitled or subject to the property, rights or liabilities under an agreement to which he was then a party.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies—

P3para.Text: whether or not the agreement is in writing;
whether or not the transferor could assign the property, rights or liabilities.

P2para.Text: So far as the agreement relates to the property, rights or liabilities transferred to the transferee, as respects anything falling to be done after the coming into force of the scheme the agreement is to have effect as if—

P3para.Text: the transferee had been a party to it instead of the transferor;
a reference to the transferor were a reference to the transferee;

a reference to a person employed by (or engaged in the business of) the transferor and holding a specified office or serving in a specified capacity were a reference to such a person as the transferee may appoint or, in default of appointment, to a person with corresponding functions who is employed by (or engaged in the business of) the transferee;

a reference in general terms to persons employed by, persons engaged in the business of, or agents of, the transferor were a reference to persons employed by, persons engaged in the business of, or agents of, the transferee.

P2para.Text: A reference mentioned in sub-paragraph (3)(b) or (c) may be express or implied; and if express it is immaterial how it is worded.
It is immaterial how a reference mentioned in sub-paragraph (3)(d) is worded.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: a transfer scheme provides for the transfer of property, rights or liabilities from a transferor to a transferee, and

immediately before the coming into force of the scheme any provision of an agreement to which the transferor was not a party, any statutory provision or any provisions of a document (other than an agreement) related to the property, rights or liabilities transferred to the transferee.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies—

P3para.Text: whether or not the agreement mentioned in sub-paragraph (1)(b) is in writing;
whether or not the transferor could assign the property, rights or liabilities.

P2para.Text: So far as the agreement, provision or document relates to the property, rights or liabilities transferred to the transferee, as respects anything falling to be done after the coming into force of the scheme the agreement, provision or document is to have effect as if—

P3para.Text: a reference to the transferor were a reference to the transferee;

a reference to a person employed by (or engaged in the business of) the transferor and holding a specified office or serving in a specified capacity were a reference to such a person as the transferee may appoint or, in default of appointment, to a person with corresponding functions who is employed by (or engaged in the business of) the transferee;

a reference in general terms to persons employed by, persons engaged in the business of, or agents of, the transferor were a reference to persons employed by, persons engaged in the business of, or agents of, the transferee.

P2para.Text: A reference mentioned in sub-paragraph (3)(a) or (b) may be express or implied; and if express it is immaterial how it is worded.
It is immaterial how a reference mentioned in sub-paragraph (3)(c) is worded.
A reference mentioned in sub-paragraph (3) to the transferor may be a general reference to a class of persons of which the transferor is one (without the transferor being named).
For the purposes of this paragraph a statutory provision is a provision contained in an Act or in a document made or issued under an Act; and here “Act” includes a private or local Act.
This paragraph applies if a transfer scheme provides for a transfer from a transferor to a transferee.

From the coming into force of the scheme the transferee is to have the same rights, powers and remedies for ascertaining, perfecting or enforcing a right or liability transferred to him under the scheme as he would have had if the right or liability had at all times been a right or liability of his.

From the coming into force of the scheme any person (other than the transferee) is to have the same rights, powers and remedies for ascertaining, perfecting or enforcing a right or liability transferred to the transferee under the scheme as he would have had if the right or liability had at all times been a right or liability of the transferee.
The rights and powers which the transferee or any other person is to have include—

P3para.Text: rights and powers as to the taking or resisting of legal proceedings;
rights and powers as to the making or resisting of applications to an authority.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (6) applies if on the coming into force of the scheme legal proceedings or applications to an authority by or against the transferor are pending.
The proceedings or applications must be continued by or against the transferee (to the transferor’s exclusion) in so far as they relate—

P3para.Text: to any property, rights or liabilities transferred to the transferee under the scheme, or
to any agreement or enactment relating to any such property, rights or liabilities.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: an agreement is made by the parties under paragraph 5 or 9 or treated as made under paragraph 6 or 10, or
an instrument is executed by the parties under paragraph 9.

P2para.Text: The agreement or instrument is to bind all other persons even if it would (apart from this sub-paragraph) have required the consent or concurrence of any other person.

If as a result of the agreement or instrument the rights or liabilities of a person who is not a party become enforceable as to part against or by one party and as to part against or by another party—

P3para.Text: the parties must notify that person of the agreement or instrument;
that person may within the period of 28 days (starting with the day he is notified) apply to the Secretary of State to give a direction to vary the agreement or instrument.

P2para.Text: If the Secretary of State is satisfied that the agreement or instrument operated unfairly against that person, the Secretary of State may give a direction to the parties requiring them to vary the agreement or instrument in a way specified in the direction.
For the purposes of this paragraph—

P3para.Text: a party is a person who is a transferor or a transferee under the transfer scheme or schemes referred to in this paragraph;
a third party is a person who is not a transferor or a transferee under the transfer scheme or schemes referred to in this paragraph.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: a transfer scheme is made or transfer schemes are made,
rights or liabilities of a third party are (apart from the scheme or schemes) enforceable against or by a transferor,
in consequence of the scheme or schemes or of anything done under this Schedule the third party’s rights or liabilities become enforceable as to different parts against or by different parties, and
the value of any property or interest of the third party is diminished as a result.

P2para.Text: Just compensation must be paid to the third party by one or more of these persons—

P3para.Text: the parties against or by whom the third party’s rights or liabilities become enforceable;
the transferor concerned (if he does not fall within paragraph (a)).

P2para.Text: If it appears to the transferor that a person is or may be entitled to compensation the transferor must—

P3para.Text: notify the person that he is or may be entitled, and
invite him to make representations to the transferor within the period of 14 days starting with the date the notification is made.

P2para.Text: But if the transferor does not know the person’s name and address he must instead publish (in a manner he thinks is appropriate) a notice which—

P3para.Text: contains information about the property or interest affected, and

invites any person who thinks he is or may be entitled to compensation to make representations to the transferor within the period specified in the notice (which must not be less than 28 days starting with the date of publication of the notice).

P2para.Text: A dispute about whether (or how much) compensation is payable under this paragraph, or about who must pay or be paid it, must be referred to and determined by—

P3para.Text: an arbitrator appointed by the President of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (if the proceedings are to be held in England and Wales),
an arbiter appointed by the Chairman of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors in Scotland (if the proceedings are to be held in Scotland), or
an arbitrator appointed by the Chairman of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors in Northern Ireland (if the proceedings are to be held in Northern Ireland).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this paragraph—

P3para.Text: a third party is a person who is not a transferor or a transferee under the transfer scheme or schemes referred to in this paragraph;

a transferred item is any property, right, liability, undertaking or part of an undertaking which is the subject of a transfer (or transfers) under the transfer scheme or schemes referred to in this paragraph.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if a transfer scheme is made (or transfer schemes are made) and there are court proceedings the parties to which are (or include) a third party and either—

P3para.Text: the transferor of a transferred item, or
any transferee or transferees of the item.

P2para.Text: The third party may apply to the court at any stage in the proceedings on any of these grounds—

P3para.Text: that the issues in the proceedings depend on the identification, with regard to the transferred item, of what has been transferred to whom and what (if anything) has been retained and that the identification has not yet been made;

that the issues in the proceedings raise a question of construction on the provisions of this Chapter which would not arise if the transferor of the transferred item and the transferee (or transferees) of it constituted a single person.

P2para.Text: If it appears to the court that such a ground is established it may hear and determine the proceedings on the first and second bases set out below.
If the transferor of the transferred item is a party to the proceedings, the first basis is that the transferor represents and is answerable for the transferee (or transferees) of the item.
If there is one transferee of the transferred item and he is a party to the proceedings, the first basis is that the transferee represents and is answerable for the transferor of the item.

If there are two or more transferees of the transferred item and they are parties to the proceedings, the first basis is that the transferees represent and are answerable for the transferor of the item.
If there are two or more transferees of the transferred item and one or more of them (but not both or all of them) are parties to the proceedings, the first basis is that—

P3para.Text: the transferee who is a party represents and is answerable for the transferor of the item and for the transferee of it who is not (or the transferees of it who are not) parties, or
the transferees who are parties represent and are answerable for the transferor of the item and for the transferee of it who is not (or the transferees of it who are not) parties.

P2para.Text: The second basis is that the transferor of the transferred item and the transferee (or transferees) of it constitute a single person.
If the court determines the proceedings on the first and second bases any judgment or order of the court is to bind both the transferor and the transferee (or transferees) of the transferred item.
For the purposes of this paragraph a relevant person is a person who satisfies these conditions—

P3para.Text: he is a transferor or transferee under a transfer scheme or transfer schemes, and
he might be prejudiced by paragraph 21 if there were court proceedings in which the scheme or schemes were an issue.

P2para.Text: A relevant person must keep each other relevant person informed of any court proceedings in which the scheme or schemes may become an issue.
This paragraph applies if a person falling within sub-paragraph (3) (the claimant) claims that—

P3para.Text: he has been prejudiced by paragraph 21,
another person or other persons falling within sub-paragraph (3) ought to indemnify him, and
there has been an unreasonable failure by the person (or any of the persons) to indemnify him.

P2para.Text: The claimant may refer the matter to the Secretary of State for determination by him; and a determination must be complied with.
A person falls within this sub-paragraph if he is a transferor or a transferee under the scheme or schemes concerned.

P1para.Text: Paragraphs 11 to 18 and 20 apply whether or not property, rights or liabilities are (or are to be) transferred under the scheme or schemes as a constituent of an undertaking (or part of one).

P2para.Text: Paragraphs 12 to 18 and 20 to 24 have effect as if references to a transfer scheme or schemes included references to—

P3para.Text: an agreement or agreements under paragraph 9 or 11;
an instrument or instruments under paragraph 9;
an agreement or agreements treated as made under paragraph 10.

P2para.Text: Where paragraph 14 has effect in relation to an agreement under paragraph 11 by virtue of sub-paragraph (1), sub-paragraph (2)(b) of paragraph 14 shall be disregarded.
Paragraph 19 has effect in relation to an agreement under paragraph 11 as it has effect in relation to an agreement made under paragraph 5 or 9.
Where paragraphs 12 to 24 have effect in relation to—

P3para.Text: an agreement under paragraph 9 or 11,
an instrument under paragraph 9, or
an agreement treated as made under paragraph 10,

P2para.Text: references to a transferor or a transferee have effect as references to a transferor or a transferee under the agreement or the instrument.

TitleBlock.Title: Transfer schemes: tax

P1para.Text: In this Schedule—

Para.Text: “the 1988 Act” means the Income and Corporation Taxes Act 1988;
“the 1990 Act” means the Capital Allowances Act 1990;
“the 1992 Act” means the Taxation of Chargeable Gains Act 1992;
“relevant transfer” means a transfer of property, rights or liabilities under a transfer scheme;
“transferee” in relation to a relevant transfer means the person to whom the property, rights or liabilities are transferred;
“transferor” in relation to a relevant transfer means the person from whom the property, rights or liabilities are transferred.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the 1992 Act a disposal constituted by a relevant transfer is to be taken (in relation to the transferee as well as the transferor) to be for a consideration such that no gain or loss accrues to the transferor.
Sub-paragraph (1) has effect subject to the following provisions of this Schedule.

Section 171(1) of the 1992 Act (provision in relation to disposal of assets from one member of a group of companies to another member of the group) does not apply if the disposal in question is constituted by a relevant transfer.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that Act.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: assets are transferred to a company under a transfer scheme,
in consequence the Secretary of State gives a direction under section 49 above, and
the company issues securities in accordance with the direction.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the 1992 Act the person to whom the securities are issued is to be treated as acquiring them for a consideration—

P3para.Text: provided by him wholly and exclusively for the securities, and
equal to the market value of the assets transferred to the company under the scheme.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies whether or not the person to whom the securities are issued is the person transferring the assets under the scheme.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that Act.
This paragraph applies if —

P3para.Text: the Secretary of State gives a direction under section 57 above requiring the CAA to release a company from liability in respect of debts,
in connection with the direction the Secretary of State gives a direction or directions under section 58 above, and
securities are issued in accordance with the direction or directions under section 58.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (3) applies if the direction under section 58 requires securities to be issued to one person only or the directions under that section (taken together) require securities to be issued to one person only; and sub-paragraph (4) applies in any other case.
For the purposes of the 1992 Act the person to whom the securities are issued is to be treated as acquiring them for a consideration—

P3para.Text: provided by him wholly and exclusively for the securities, and
equal to the amount of the liability affected by the release required by the direction under section 57.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the 1992 Act a person to whom any of the securities are issued is to be treated as acquiring them for a consideration—

P3para.Text: provided by him wholly and exclusively for the securities, and
equal to such part as is just and reasonable of the amount of the liability affected by the release required by the direction under section 57.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies whether or not the person to whom the securities are issued, or any person to whom any of the securities are issued, is a person transferring anything under the transfer scheme in connection with which the direction under section 57 is given.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that Act.

P1para.Text: Nothing in this Chapter and nothing done under it is to be regarded as a scheme or arrangement for the purposes of section 30 of the 1992 Act (tax-free benefits).

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: but for section 154 of the 1992 Act (depreciating assets) a held-over gain would have been carried forward to a depreciating asset,
the asset is the subject of a relevant transfer, and
the Secretary of State is not the transferee under the relevant transfer.

P2para.Text: Section 154 is to have effect as if the gain had accrued to, and the claim for it to be held over had been made by, the transferee and as if the transferor’s acquisition of the depreciating asset had been the transferee’s acquisition of it.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in section 154 have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that section.

If there has been a relevant transfer of an asset section 174(1) of the 1992 Act (which applies section 41 to cases where assets have been acquired without gain or loss) is to have effect as if the asset had been transferred to the transferee, and acquired by him, in relevant circumstances.
This paragraph is not to prejudice paragraph 2.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in section 174(1) of the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in section 174(1).
Sub-paragraph (2) applies if a company (the degrouped company)—

P3para.Text: acquired an asset from another company at any time when both were members of the same group of companies (the old group),
ceases by virtue of a relevant transfer to be a member of the old group, and
becomes by virtue of the transfer a member of another group of companies (the new group).

P2para.Text: Section 179 of the 1992 Act (company ceasing to be member of group) is not to treat the degrouped company as having by virtue of the transfer sold and immediately reacquired the asset.
Sub-paragraph (4) applies if—

P3para.Text: sub-paragraph (2) applies to an asset, and
the degrouped company ceases to be a member of the new group.

P2para.Text: On the company so ceasing section 179 of the 1992 Act is to have effect as if the degrouped company and the company from which it acquired the asset had been members of the new group at the time of acquisition.
But sub-paragraph (4) does not apply if—

P3para.Text: at the time when the degrouped company ceases to be a member of the new group the company from which it acquired the asset also ceases to be a member of the new group,
the companies are associated companies immediately before and immediately after that time, and
the companies were associated companies at the time of acquisition.

P2para.Text: Expressions used in this paragraph and in section 179 of the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that section.
Sub-paragraph (3) applies if—

P3para.Text: a company (the degrouped company) ceases by virtue of a relevant transfer to be a member of a group of companies (the old group),
it becomes by virtue of the transfer a member of another group of companies (the new group),
it ceases to be a member of the new group, and
the condition in sub-paragraph (2) is satisfied.

P2para.Text: The condition is that—

P3para.Text: the degrouped company acquired an asset under a relevant transfer at a time falling before it ceases to be a member of the new group, and
at the time of acquisition the degrouped company and the transferor were not members of the new group.

P2para.Text: On the degrouped company ceasing to be a member of the new group section 179 of the 1992 Act is to have effect as if the degrouped company and the transferor had been members of the new group at the time of acquisition.
But sub-paragraph (3) does not apply if—

P3para.Text: at the time when the degrouped company ceases to be a member of the new group the transferor also ceases to be a member of the new group,
the companies are associated companies immediately before and immediately after that time, and
the companies were associated companies at the time of acquisition.

P2para.Text: Paragraph 8(4) and sub-paragraph (3) above may apply on the same occasion; but if paragraph 8(4) applies to an asset on a given occasion sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to that asset on that occasion.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in section 179 of the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that section.
Sub-paragraph (4) applies if—

P3para.Text: a company ceases by virtue of a relevant transfer to be a member of a group of companies (the old group),
it becomes by virtue of the transfer a member of another group of companies (the new group),
a company falling within sub-paragraph (2) (the degrouped company) ceases to be a member of the new group, and
the condition in sub-paragraph (3) is satisfied.

P2para.Text: A company falls within this sub-paragraph if immediately before it ceases to be a member of the new group it is a subsidiary of—

P3para.Text: the company referred to in sub-paragraph (1)(a), or
the principal company of the new group (if that company differs from the company referred to in sub-paragraph (1)(a)).

P2para.Text: The condition is that—

P3para.Text: the degrouped company acquired an asset under a relevant transfer at a time falling before it ceases to be a member of the new group, and
at the time of acquisition the degrouped company and the transferor were not members of the new group.

P2para.Text: On the degrouped company ceasing to be a member of the new group section 179 of the 1992 Act is to have effect as if the degrouped company and the transferor had been members of the new group at the time of acquisition.
But sub-paragraph (4) does not apply if—

P3para.Text: at the time when the degrouped company ceases to be a member of the new group the transferor also ceases to be a member of the new group,
the companies are associated companies immediately before and immediately after that time, and
the companies were associated companies at the time of acquisition.

P2para.Text: Expressions used in this paragraph and in section 179 of the 1992 Act have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that section.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: property which is plant or machinery is the subject of a relevant transfer,
Chapter 1 of Part 22 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 (transfers of trade without a change of ownership) does not apply in relation to the transfer, and

the transfer scheme concerned contains provision for the disposal value of the property to be taken for the purposes of the Capital Allowances Acts to be of an amount specified in or determined in accordance with the scheme.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the Capital Allowances Acts—

P3para.Text: the provision mentioned in sub-paragraph (1)(c) is to have effect (instead of section 26(1) or 59 of the 1990 Act) for determining an amount as the disposal value of the property or the price at which a fixture is to be treated as sold;
the transferee is to be taken to have incurred expenditure of that amount on the provision of the property;

in the case of a fixture, the expenditure which falls to be treated as incurred by the transferee is to be taken for the purposes of section 54 of the 1990 Act to be incurred by the giving of a consideration consisting in a capital sum of that amount.

P2para.Text: A provision mentioned in sub-paragraph (1)(c) for the determination of an amount may include provision—

P3para.Text: for a determination to be made by the Secretary of State in a manner described in the scheme;
for a determination to be made by reference to factors so described or to the opinion of a person so described;
for a determination to be capable of being modified (on one or more occasions) in a manner and in circumstances so described.

P2para.Text: The Treasury’s consent is required for the making or modification of a determination under a provision mentioned in sub-paragraph (1)(c).
The transferee’s consent is also required for such a modification after the relevant transfer takes effect.
If there is a determination or a modification of a determination under a provision mentioned in sub-paragraph (1)(c) all necessary adjustments—

P3para.Text: must be made by making assessments or by repayment or discharge of tax, and
must be made notwithstanding any limitation on the time within which assessments may be made.

P2para.Text: In this paragraph “the Capital Allowances Acts” has the same meaning as in the Tax Acts and “fixture” has the same meaning as in Chapter VI of Part II of the 1990 Act.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: under a relevant transfer trading stock of the transferor is transferred to the transferee, and
the stock falls, immediately after the time when the transfer takes effect, to be treated as trading stock of the transferee.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraphs (3) and (4) have effect in computing the profits or gains of the relevant trades for the purposes of the Corporation Tax Acts; and the relevant trades are—

P3para.Text: the trade in relation to which the stock is trading stock immediately before the time when the transfer takes effect, and
the trade in relation to which it is trading stock after that time.

P2para.Text: The stock must be taken—

P3para.Text: to have been disposed of by the transferor in the course of the trade carried on by the transferor,
to have been acquired by the transferee in the course of the trade carried on by the transferee, and
subject to that, to have been disposed of and acquired at the time when the transfer takes effect.

P2para.Text: The stock must be valued for the purposes of each of the relevant trades as if the disposal and acquisition had been for a consideration which in relation to the transferor would have resulted in neither a profit nor a loss being brought into account in respect of the disposal in the accounting period of the transferor which ends with, or is current at, the time when the transfer takes effect.
In this paragraph “trading stock” has the same meaning as in section 163 of the Corporation Tax Act 2009.
This paragraph applies if a transfer scheme provides for a relevant transfer as a result of which the transferor ceases to carry on a trade and the transferee begins to carry it on.

A transferor treated as ceasing to carry on a trade for the purposes of Chapter 1 of Part 22 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 (transfers of trade without a change of ownership) is to be so treated for the purposes of this paragraph.
A transferee treated as beginning to carry on a trade for the purposes of that Chapter is to be so treated for the purposes of this paragraph.

Sub-paragraph (5) applies if the transfer will result in the transferee being entitled to relief for an amount in respect of the trade under section 45 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 (carry forward of trading losses) by virtue of section 944(3) of that Act.
In such a case the scheme may provide that the amount is to be treated as such amount (the replacement amount) as is specified in or determined in accordance with the scheme.

Sub-paragraph (7) applies if the trade concerned is in fact part of a trade of the transferor and the transferor is entitled to relief for an amount under section 45 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 in respect of the part retained.
In such a case the scheme may provide that the amount is to be treated as such amount (the replacement amount) as is specified in or determined in accordance with the scheme.
A provision under sub-paragraph (5) or (7) must be such that the replacement amount is not greater than the amount it replaces; and the replacement amount may be nil.
When the scheme comes into force a provision made under sub-paragraph (5) or (7) is to have effect for the purposes of arriving at the amount of relief concerned.
This paragraph applies if under a relevant transfer all the issued share capital of a company (the transferred company) is transferred from the CAA to—

P3para.Text: the Secretary of State, or
a company whose shares are all held by the Secretary of State when the transfer takes effect.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of Chapter 2 of Part 14 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 (but not section 674(1) of that Act) (disallowance of trading losses on change in company’s ownership) the transfer is not to be taken to result in a change in the ownership of—

P3para.Text: the transferred company, or
a company which is a wholly owned subsidiary of the transferred company when the transfer takes effect.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of Chapter 4 of Part 19 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 or Chapter 4 of Part 12A of the Income Tax Act 2007 (assets leased to traders and others) if the interest of the lessor or the lessee under a lease, or any other interest in an asset, is transferred to a person under a relevant transfer.

The transfer is to be treated as made without any capital sum having been obtained in respect of the interest by the transferor or the transferee; and this is so notwithstanding section 879 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 and section 681DI of the Income Tax Act 2007.
This paragraph applies if securities are issued by a company in pursuance of a direction of the Secretary of State under section 49 or 58 above.

A share issued by the company is to be treated for the purposes of the Corporation Tax Acts as if it had been issued wholly in consideration of a subscription paid to the company of an amount equal to the nominal value of the share.
A debenture issued by the company is to be treated for the purposes of the Corporation Tax Acts as if it had been issued—

P3para.Text: wholly in consideration of a loan made to the company of an amount equal to the principal sum payable under the debenture, and
wholly and exclusively for the purposes of the trade carried on by the company.

P2para.Text: If a debenture issued by the company includes provision for the payment of a sum expressed as interest in respect of a period falling wholly or partly before the issue of the debenture, a payment made in pursuance of the provision in respect of the period is to be treated for the purposes of the Corporation Tax Acts as if the debenture had been issued at the commencement of the period and (accordingly) as interest on the principal sum payable under the debenture.
This paragraph has effect subject to paragraphs 3, 4 and 17.
This paragraph applies if—

P3para.Text: securities are issued to a company in pursuance of a direction of the Secretary of State under section 49 or 58 above, and
by virtue of any such security the company has a loan relationship for the purposes of the Corporation Tax Acts.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of Part 5 of the Corporation Tax Act 2009 (loan relationships) the company is to be taken to have acquired its rights under the security wholly in consideration of a loan made by it to the issuing company of an amount equal to the principal sum payable under the security.
Expressions used in this paragraph and in Part 5 of the Corporation Tax Act 2009 have the same meanings in this paragraph as in that Part.
A relevant transfer is not to give rise to liability to stamp duty.
Stamp duty is not to be chargeable on a transfer scheme.

Stamp duty is not to be chargeable on an instrument which is certified to the Commissioners of Inland Revenue by the Secretary of State as having been made for the purposes of (or for purposes connected with) a transfer scheme.
But no instrument which is certified as mentioned in sub-paragraph (3) is to be taken to be duly stamped unless—

P3para.Text: it is stamped with the duty to which it would be liable but for that sub-paragraph, or
it has, in accordance with section 12 of the Stamp Act 1891, been stamped with a particular stamp denoting that it is not chargeable with that duty or that it is duly stamped.

P2para.Text: Stamp duty is not to be chargeable on an instrument which is made under Schedule 6.

P1para.Text: An agreement is not to give rise to a charge to stamp duty reserve tax if—

P3para.Text: it is made for the purposes of (or for purposes connected with) a transfer scheme, or
it is made under Schedule 6.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (2) applies if the effect of—

P3para.Text: an agreement made under paragraph 9 or 11 of Schedule 6,
an instrument executed under paragraph 9 of Schedule 6, or
an agreement treated as made under paragraph 10 of Schedule 6,

P2para.Text: is to modify the effect of a transfer scheme.
This Schedule, the 1988 Act, the 1990 Act and the 1992 Act are to have effect as if—

P3para.Text: the scheme had been made as modified, and

anything done by or in relation to the preceding holder had (so far as relating to the property, rights or liabilities affected by the modification) been done by or in relation to the subsequent holder.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (4) applies to a disposal of an asset if the disposal—

P3para.Text: is effected in pursuance of an agreement made or treated as made under paragraph 9 or 10 of Schedule 6 or is effected by an instrument executed under paragraph 9 of that Schedule, and
is the grant of a lease of land or the creation of other rights and liabilities over land.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the 1992 Act the disposal is to be taken (in relation to the person to whom it is made as well as the person making it) to be for a consideration such that no gain or loss accrues to the person making it.

Section 171(1) of the 1992 Act (provision in relation to disposal of assets from one member of a group of companies to another member of the group) does not apply if sub-paragraph (4) applies to the disposal in question.
References in this paragraph to an agreement or instrument include references to the agreement or instrument as varied in accordance with a direction under paragraph 19(4) of Schedule 6.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (2) the preceding holder is the person who without the modification—

P3para.Text: became (under the transfer scheme concerned) entitled or subject to the property, rights or liabilities affected by the modification, or
remained (despite the transfer scheme concerned) entitled or subject to the property, rights or liabilities affected by the modification,

P2para.Text: as the case may be.

For the purposes of sub-paragraph (2) the subsequent holder is the person who (in consequence of the modification) becomes, or resumes being, entitled or subject to the property, rights or liabilities affected by the modification.

TitleBlock.Title: Amendments about air traffic

P1para.Text: In the House of Commons Disqualification Act 1975, in Part III of Schedule 1, after the entry “Director of the Commonwealth Institute” there shall be inserted—

P2para.Text: Director of any of the following—

P3para.Text: a company which for the time being holds a licence under Chapter I of Part I of the Transport Act 2000 (a licence company);
a company of which a licence company is a subsidiary (within the meaning given by section 736(1) of the Companies Act 1985 or Article 4(1) of the Companies (Northern Ireland) Order 1986);
a company which is a subsidiary (within the meaning so given) of a licence company.

P1para.Text: In the Northern Ireland Assembly Disqualification Act 1975, in Part III of Schedule 1, after the entry “Director of Cable and Wireless Limited nominated by a Minister of the Crown or government department” there shall be inserted—

P2para.Text: Director of any of the following—

P3para.Text: a company which for the time being holds a licence under Chapter I of Part I of the Transport Act 2000 (a licence company);
a company of which a licence company is a subsidiary (within the meaning given by section 736(1) of the Companies Act 1985 or Article 4(1) of the Companies (Northern Ireland) Order 1986);
a company which is a subsidiary (within the meaning so given) of a licence company.

P1para.Text: Section 72 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (CAA’s duty to provide air navigation services) shall cease to have effect.
Sections 73 and 74 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (charges for air navigation services etc) shall cease to have effect.

In section 86 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (mortgaging of aircraft) in subsection (2)(b) for “section 74(4) above” there shall be substituted “ section 83 of the Transport Act 2000 (detention and sale of aircraft) ”.

P2para.Text: Section 88 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (detention and sale of aircraft for unpaid airport charges) shall be amended as follows.

In subsection (6)(d) for “regulations under section 73 above” substitute “ section 73 of the Transport Act 2000 (or, if more than one such charge is due, in payment of them in such order as the Secretary of State may specify by order) ”.
In subsection (10) in the definition of “airport charges” for “regulations under section 73 above” substitute “ section 73 of the Transport Act 2000 ”.

P1para.Text: In section 90 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (Convention rights) in subsection (2)(b) for “section 74(4) above” there shall be substituted “ section 83 of the Transport Act 2000 (detention and sale of aircraft) ”.

P2para.Text: In Schedule 4 to the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (Eurocontrol) paragraph 1 shall be amended as follows.
In sub-paragraph (5) omit the definition of “record”.
After sub-paragraph (5) insert—
For the purposes of this paragraph a record includes (in addition to a record in writing)—

P3para.Text: a disc, tape, sound-track or other device in which sounds or signals are embodied so as to be capable of being reproduced from it (with or without the aid of some other instrument);
a film, tape or other device in which visual images are embodied so as to be capable of being reproduced from it (with or without the aid of some other instrument);
a photograph.

P1para.Text: In Schedule 13 to the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (subordinate instruments) in Part II after the entry relating to section 87 there shall be inserted—

tr.td: Subject to the negative resolution procedure

P1para.Text: In section 4 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (CAA’s general objectives) after subsection (2) there shall be inserted—

P2para.Text: The duty mentioned in subsection (1) above does not apply in relation to anything done by the CAA in the performance of functions mentioned in subsection (3) of section 86 of the Transport Act 2000 which, by virtue of that section, are concurrent functions of the CAA and the Director General of Fair Trading.

However, when performing such a function the CAA may have regard to any matter in respect of which a duty is imposed by subsection (1) above if it is a matter to which the Director General of Fair Trading could have regard when performing that function.
Section 54 of the Competition Act 1998 (regulators) shall be amended as follows.
In subsection (4) after “Schedule 10” insert “ or by Chapter V of Part I of the Transport Act 2000 ”.
Schedule 13 to the Competition Act 1998 (transitionals and savings) shall be amended as follows.
In paragraph 1(1) in the definition of “regulator” after “Schedule 10” insert “ and the Civil Aviation Authority ”.
In paragraph 35(2) after paragraph (g) insert—

P3para.Text: in the case of the Civil Aviation Authority, the supply of air traffic services within the meaning given by section 98 of the Transport Act 2000.

P2para.Text: Section 6 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (directions in national interest etc) shall be amended as follows.
In each of subsections (1) and (2) omit the words from “and in so far” to the end.
After subsection (2) insert—

In so far as any directions given under this section conflict with the requirements of section 93 of the Transport Act 2000 or of an order under section 94 of that Act, the directions shall be disregarded.

In so far as any directions given under this section conflict with the requirements of any enactment or instrument relating to the CAA (other than section 93 of the Transport Act 2000 or an order under section 94 of that Act) the requirements shall be disregarded.

P1para.Text: Sections 62 and 63 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 (control in time of war or emergency) shall cease to have effect.

P2para.Text: Section 30 of the Airports Act 1986 (directions in interests of national security etc) shall be amended as follows.
After subsection (4) insert—

In so far as any direction applying to an airport operator by virtue of subsection (1), (2) or (3) conflicts with the requirements of section 93 of the Transport Act 2000 or of an order under section 94 of that Act, the direction shall be disregarded.
In subsection (5) after “to him as an airport operator” insert “ (other than section 93 of the Transport Act 2000 or an order under section 94 of that Act) ”.

TitleBlock.Title: Air traffic: information

P2para.Text: This Schedule applies to information if—

P3para.Text: it was obtained under or by virtue of this Part, and
it relates to the affairs of an individual or to a particular business.

P2para.Text: The information must not be disclosed during the lifetime of the individual or so long as the business is carried on, except as provided below.

P1para.Text: Paragraph 1(2) does not apply to a disclosure made with the consent of the individual or the person for the time being carrying on the business.

P2para.Text: Paragraph 1(2) does not apply to a disclosure made—

P3para.Text: for the purpose of facilitating the carrying out by the Secretary of State, the CAA or the Competition and Markets Authority of any of his or their functions under this Part;
for the purpose of facilitating the carrying out by a person or body mentioned in sub-paragraph (2) of any of his or its functions under an enactment or instrument specified in sub-paragraph (3);

for the purpose of enabling or assisting the Secretary of State or the Treasury to exercise any powers conferred by the Financial Services Act 1986 or by the enactments relating to companies, insurance companies or insolvency;
for the purpose of enabling or assisting an inspector appointed under the enactments relating to companies to carry out his functions;
